questions_and_answers.question: Can Zerodha delete client data on request?
questions_and_answers.answer: No, Zerodha cannot permanently delete client data on request. SEBI regulations require brokers to retain client documents for at least 8 years for audit and review purposes.

questions_and_answers.question: How to close the Zerodha account?
questions_and_answers.answer:
You cannot close your account if you have a negative balance. All positions must be squared off, and holdings must be sold or transferred before closure. You can choose closure-cum-transfer. Download necessary reports from console.zerodha.com before closing, as they won't be accessible afterward. You cannot reopen the same account with the same User ID.  To open a new account, see "How to open a Zerodha account online?". Multiple account closures with the same PAN may lead to application rejection.

**Online Closure (Resident Indians, NRIs, minors with Kite access):** Log in to console.zerodha.com, click Account, then Segments, then Close account. Select a reason, provide feedback, click Continue, accept terms, click Proceed to eSign, then Sign now. Authorize NSDL, enter Aadhaar number, and verify the OTP.

**Offline Closure (Joint accounts, minors without Kite access, commodity account only closure):** Create a ticket with the e-signed account closure form.  Joint account holders and minors require all holders'/guardian's signatures. 

**Offline Closure (Non-individual accounts):** Complete the account closure form and courier it to Zerodha's Bengaluru address.  Authorized signatories must sign for corporate, OPC, LLP, partnership, trust, AOP, and HUF accounts.

Account closure takes 3 working days; a confirmation email will be sent.  The account can be temporarily deactivated using Kill Switch.

questions_and_answers.question: Does Zerodha share customer data with regulatory tech companies?
questions_and_answers.answer: Zerodha prioritizes customer data security and does not share customer data directly with regulatory tech companies. While Zerodha uses TSS Consultancy Pvt. Ltd. for AML and PMLA regulatory alerts,  Zerodha self-hosts TSS's database and manages the server setup, maintaining full control over customer data.  All necessary regulatory checks are performed within this setup.

questions_and_answers.question: How to verify if a call is officially from Zerodha?
questions_and_answers.answer: Zerodha will only call you regarding account opening issues, margin calls, or compliance matters; they will never ask for sensitive information or provide stock tips.  Calls will only come from the following numbers: 080 37074647, 080 37096498, 080 37096499, 080 71173891, 080 47186626, 080 71173861, 080 71909543, 080 71909545, 080 37074651, 080 71966807, 080 47192020, 080 47092457, 080 47181888, 080 47181999, 080 47169000, 080 47184927, 080 46805727. If you receive a call from a different number claiming to be from Zerodha, ignore it, create a support ticket with the number, and consider reporting it to TRAI. Zerodha uses 951 351 2020 for WhatsApp OTPs/messages.

questions_and_answers.question: Why does Zerodha email a weekly statement?
questions_and_answers.answer: As per exchange regulations (ZIP), stockbrokers must send weekly ledger statements and security registers to clients. These statements detail fund transactions and holdings, including pending obligations (unsettled trades).  An example scenario illustrates how trades from the last trading day of the week appear as pending obligations in the following week's statement.

questions_and_answers.question: Why did Zerodha send an email requesting certain documents to be resubmitted?
questions_and_answers.answer: Zerodha may request resubmission of documents to ensure validity and compliance with SEBI regulations (WEB). Submit the documents via a support ticket within 30 days; otherwise, your account will be blocked.  For more information, see "Why did Zerodha send an email asking for KYC information?". Account unblocking takes up to 48 hours after document submission.

questions_and_answers.question: Why did Zerodha send an email requesting KYC details to be updated?
questions_and_answers.answer: Per NSE (PDF) and BSE (WEB) circulars, accounts with 12 months of inactivity are marked for re-KYC. To reactivate, log in to signup.zerodha.com/rekyc, click Continue with Kite, and either proceed with existing details, update your address, or update non-compliant details.  You may need to upload income proof for F&O trading, update your FATCA declaration, and complete In-Person Verification (IPV). Reactivation takes 24-48 hours.  Offline address updates are needed if your mobile number isn't Aadhaar-linked.  Dormant accounts receive dividends but require KYC reactivation for buybacks, OFS, rights issues, etc.  Even IPO, corporate action, or mutual fund orders don't prevent dormancy. NRIs and non-individuals must send physical documents for address changes.

questions_and_answers.question: Why was an email and SMS sent by the clearing corporation informing about the allocation of funds?
questions_and_answers.answer: As per SEBI guidelines (WEB), brokers must allocate client funds segment-wise to the Clearing Corporation (CC). The CC's email and SMS inform clients of this allocation; no action is required from the client.  Example scenarios illustrate how funds are allocated based on trading activity and margin usage.  If no trades are placed, 100% of the cash margin is allocated to the EQ segment, but clients can still use these funds across segments.

questions_and_answers.question: Why does Zerodha not allow users to register with Rediffmail email IDs?
questions_and_answers.answer: Zerodha restricts Rediffmail IDs due to increased cyberattacks targeting Rediff accounts and the frequent non-delivery of emails to Rediffmail addresses.  It's recommended to change your email address if you've already registered with a Rediffmail ID.

questions_and_answers.question: Why did the KYC Registration Agency (KRA) send an email and SMS informing about KYC details validation?
questions_and_answers.answer: KRAs validate client KYC details per SEBI guidelines.  The email and SMS confirm successful KYC registration. If your KYC is already validated, the status may take up to 72 hours to update. To check your KYC status and registered KRA, see "What is Know Your Customer(KYC), and how can the KYC status be checked?".  You can validate your details on the KRA website. Click the link in the email and validate your email address; check spam/trash folders if needed.  SMS delivery requires an active, non-DND mobile number; create a ticket if needed. NRIs must validate their email, and Indian mobile numbers if registered with the KRA. You can also validate your Aadhaar details on the KRA website. For incorrect details, you'll need to perform a ReKYC.

questions_and_answers.question: How to verify if the email from Zerodha is genuine?
questions_and_answers.answer: To verify the authenticity of an email from Zerodha, check the second half of the email address.  Legitimate Zerodha emails are sent only from the following domains: zerodha.com, reportsmailer.zerodha.net, mailer.zerodha.net, coinmailer.zerodha.net, intranet.zerodha.net, nbfcmailer.zerodha.net, omsmailer.zerodha.net, qmailer.zerodha.net, newslettermailer.zerodha.net, newsletters.rainmatter.com, alertsmailer.zerodha.net, newsletter.zerodha.net. Report any emails from other addresses by creating a support ticket.

questions_and_answers.question: Why did Zerodha send an email asking for bank proof?
questions_and_answers.answer: Zerodha needs to verify your linked bank account per regulations. While penny drop verification is usually used during account opening and bank detail changes, it may fail. To update the records, submit a recent bank statement, passbook, or cancelled check via a support ticket.

questions_and_answers.question: Why did Zerodha send an email stating the mobile number is blocked?
questions_and_answers.answer: Per SEBI requirements, Zerodha requires an active mobile number to send account-related communications. If your number is disconnected, you'll receive an email stating that it's blocked. To update your number, see "How to change the registered mobile number or email address with Zerodha?"

questions_and_answers.question: Why did Zerodha send an email to authorise holdings?
questions_and_answers.answer: If you haven't submitted a Power of Attorney (POA) or Demat Debit and Pledge Instruction (DDPI), you must authorize the sale of securities using a CDSL TPIN before trading.  Zerodha sends authorization requests after trades are placed if: a physically settled F&O position requires stock delivery; or you couldn't square off an MIS sell position due to an upper circuit limit. Authorize holdings via the email link before 7:00 PM.

questions_and_answers.question: How to update the resident status of PAN for an NRI & PIO account?
questions_and_answers.answer: To avoid trading blocks on NSE and BSE, update your residential status on the Income Tax Department (ITD) website by February 24th, 2024.  Since July 1st, 2023, the ITD has deactivated PANs not linked to Aadhaar, including those of NRIs and PIOs without updated residential status. Failure to update may result in higher TDS. Submit these documents to your Jurisdictional Assessing Officer (JAO): PAN card copy; passport copy showing NRI status, PIO card copy, OCI card copy, or other national ID/taxpayer ID (attested by Indian embassy/high commission/consulate or authorized officials of Indian banks). Find your JAO at incometax.gov.in/iec/foportal (Know Your AO). Alternatively, raise a grievance on the ITD portal.  Once this is complete, log in to eportal.incometax.gov.in/iec/foservices/#/login, click My Profile, Edit, select Non-Resident, and Save.

questions_and_answers.question: How can an employer’s email address be added to a Zerodha account?
questions_and_answers.answer: To add your employer's email address, create a support ticket including a letter from your employer. The letter must be on company letterhead and include the authorized person's seal and signature.

questions_and_answers.question: Why was a notification sent for logging into Kite on a new device?
questions_and_answers.answer: You receive an email and device notification when you enter your password on a new device (before 2FA). This alerts you to a potential security risk. If you don't recognize the login, change your password immediately.  Brokers are required by NSE to store and share device details with the exchange for order placement, modification, and cancellation.  Kite web sessions on different browsers are treated as separate devices.  Consider enabling Time-based OTP for added security.

questions_and_answers.question: Why was a notification sent for entering multiple incorrect Two Factor Authentication (2FA)?
questions_and_answers.answer: After five incorrect 2FA attempts, your Zerodha account is blocked, and a notification is sent to your registered email and current device. This indicates potential password compromise. To unblock, reset your login credentials.  All active sessions are logged out after a password reset.

questions_and_answers.question: Does Zerodha send SMS alerts or notifications for trades?
questions_and_answers.answer: Zerodha itself does not send SMS trade alerts. However, the exchanges do send SMS notifications. To receive trade alerts within the Kite app, go to Client ID > Settings > Order Notifications.  The Kite app does not need to run in the background to receive these notifications.

questions_and_answers.question: Why was an email sent by CDSL informing about the blocking mechanism for payin of securities?
questions_and_answers.answer: Per SEBI guidelines, depositories must validate depository transfer instructions against Clearing Corporation (CC) obligation details.  If there's a mismatch, the transfer is rejected.  Zerodha ensures that the details match to avoid this; no client action is needed.

questions_and_answers.question: Why are emails from Zerodha not being received?
questions_and_answers.answer: You may not be receiving emails from Zerodha due to:  an almost full inbox; your email domain blocking external emails; emails being archived, deleted, or marked as spam; emails being forwarded; unauthorized access deleting emails; emails already read on a third-party client; or Zerodha blocking your email (for 30 days) due to delivery failures.

questions_and_answers.question: Why did Zerodha send an email asking to update the Tax Identification Number (TIN)?
questions_and_answers.answer: Per CVLKRA circular, you must provide an updated FATCA declaration by October 31st, 2024.  The ITD has requested Zerodha to collect valid TINs from clients with incorrect or invalid TINs to meet reporting requirements and avoid penalties. To update your TIN, log in to signup.zerodha.com/rekyc/fatca, and follow the instructions.

questions_and_answers.question: Why did CDSL send an email with the revised process for submission of off-market transfer?
questions_and_answers.answer: CDSL emailed clients to inform them of revised off-market transfer procedures (effective December 30, 2023, as per CDSL circular WEB).  Off-market transfers now require the buyer's demat account to be added as a beneficiary in the seller's account to prevent incorrect transfers.

questions_and_answers.question: Why do exchanges send a weekly SMS and email regarding funds and securities balances?
questions_and_answers.answer: As per SEBI circular, exchanges send weekly SMS and email notifications of your trading account funds to prevent fund misappropriation. The balance shown is as of the date specified, not the date of receipt, and represents the total balance across all segments, not a single exchange.  The total number of ISINs shown may be zero because this refers to the broker's pool account, not your demat account.

questions_and_answers.question: Why did Zerodha send an email seeking clarification for the reversal trades?
questions_and_answers.answer: SEBI requires stockbrokers to track and report unusual trading activity, including reversal trades. Reversal trades are suspected as non-genuine if the same client(s) or group are buyers and sellers at significantly different prices within a short time, resulting in profit for one and loss for another, especially in illiquid contracts.  Respond to the email with clarifications; your response (or lack thereof) will be reported to regulatory bodies.

questions_and_answers.question: How to reactivate the Zerodha account?
questions_and_answers.answer: Accounts inactive for 12 months are marked for re-KYC. To reactivate: Log in to signup.zerodha.com/rekyc, click Continue with Kite. If details are correct, click Proceed with same details; otherwise, update your address or non-compliant KYC details. Upload optional income proof for F&O trading, update your FATCA declaration, and complete IPV. Reactivation takes 24-48 hours (plus exchange processing time). Online address changes require an Aadhaar-linked mobile number; otherwise, use the offline process. Dormant accounts still receive dividends but need reactivation for buybacks, OFS, rights issues, etc.  Even with IPO or corporate action orders, accounts can be marked dormant. NRIs and non-individuals should send physical address update documents beforehand.

questions_and_answers.question: What is the CKYC number, and where can it be found?
questions_and_answers.answer: Your Central KYC (CKYC) number is a 14-digit ID from completing the KYC process; it's linked to your ID proof and stored electronically. To find it, log in to console.zerodha.com and click Account.

questions_and_answers.question: Why did Zerodha send an email asking for KYC information?
questions_and_answers.answer: Zerodha is required by NSE, BSE, and MCX to ensure your KYC is registered with a KYC Registration Agency (KRA) before you can trade; open positions may be squared off if KYC isn't verified.  Your KYC status may be "On Hold" or "Rejected". To check your KYC status, see "What is Know Your Customer (KYC), and how can the KYC status be checked?".  The email details how to rectify rejections (online or offline, depending on the issue).

questions_and_answers.question: What is Know Your Customer (KYC), and how can the KYC status be checked?
questions_and_answers.answer: KYC verifies your identity and details (income, profession, etc.), required by SEBI to open a trading/demat account.  To check your KYC status: Visit cvlkra.com, click KYC inquiry, enter your PAN and captcha, and click Submit. The KRA and KYC status will be shown.

questions_and_answers.question: What does KYC status mean?
questions_and_answers.answer: **Validated/Registered:** KYC is successfully registered; your Zerodha account will be unblocked within 72 hours.  **Under process:** KYC is being processed (up to 5 days).  **On-hold or rejected:** Incorrect details/documents were provided; Zerodha will contact you if additional documents are needed.  It can take up to 5 business days for updates. If your account was inactive for a year, you'll need to update your KYC details.

questions_and_answers.question: Who are Clients of Special Category (CSC), and when must they provide income proof?
questions_and_answers.answer: Per SEBI circular, Clients of Special Category (CSC) must provide income proof during account opening or re-KYC.  CSCs include: NRIs, high net worth individuals, trusts/charities/NGOs receiving donations, companies with close family shareholdings/beneficial ownership, Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), and clients with known questionable reputations.  Acceptable income proof includes: 6-month bank statement (average balance >₹10,000); latest salary slip (gross monthly >₹15,000); latest ITR acknowledgement (gross annual >₹1,20,000); latest Form 16 (gross annual >₹1,20,000); net worth certificate (value >₹10,00,000); or demat holdings statement (current value >₹10,000).

questions_and_answers.question: Why did Zerodha send an email asking for additional documents?
questions_and_answers.answer: Zerodha requests additional documents to ensure all account documents are valid and up-to-date, per SEBI circular.  The email and table below explain reasons for document rejection and required corrections.  Submit documents via a support ticket. Courier documents to Zerodha's Bengaluru address.  The KRA and exchanges will update your KYC status within 10 business days.

questions_and_answers.question: Why does Zerodha ask to redo KYC while opening an account, even though it was done while opening the bank account?
questions_and_answers.answer: Banks and brokers use different KYC processes. Banks use CKYC, while brokers use KYC registration via a KYC Registration Agency (KRA).  Zerodha performs its own KYC verification during account opening.  Key differences between KYC and CKYC are outlined in a table (KYC is SEBI-specific, PAN-based; CKYC is universal across BFSI sectors, uses a 14-digit number).

questions_and_answers.question: How to update the KYC details on Digilocker?
questions_and_answers.answer: To update your KYC details on Digilocker: Sign in to digilocker.gov.in/home, click Issued Documents, click ⋮ under your Aadhaar card, then Refresh, accept the consent, click Update, enter the OTP, and click Update again. Note that updating Digilocker does not update your KYC with Zerodha; see "Why did Zerodha send an email requesting KYC details to be updated?" for instructions on updating your KYC with Zerodha.

questions_and_answers.question: How can a voluntarily deactivated Zerodha account be reactivated?
questions_and_answers.answer:
For voluntarily deactivated accounts (not dormant accounts—see "Why did Zerodha send an email requesting KYC details to be updated?" for dormant accounts):

**Online (Aadhaar-linked mobile number):** Submit an e-signed reactivation letter (PDF) via a support ticket (see "How to eSign documents?").

**Offline:** Print the reactivation letter (PDF), fill it out, sign it, and courier it with a self-attested PAN card and address proof to Zerodha's Bengaluru address. Reactivation takes 7 business days; your Client ID remains the same, but you'll receive a new password.

If your trading account was deactivated but your demat account was closed, you'll need to fill out and submit a demat application (PDF).  If your entire Zerodha account was closed, you'll need to open a new account (see "How to open a Zerodha account online?")

questions_and_answers.question: What is Financial Action Task Force (FATF) list?
questions_and_answers.answer: The Financial Action Task Force (FATF) is a global organization combating money laundering and terrorist financing. It sets international standards and identifies countries with weak anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing (AML/CFT) measures. Zerodha does not allow account openings for clients from FATF blacklisted countries; those from grey-listed countries may open accounts subject to compliance team approval. See fatf-gafi.org/en/countries/black-and-grey-lists.html for the list of countries.  Zerodha may request additional income proof from NRIs in grey-listed countries to verify income sources.  This is per FATF and SEBI directives.  Acceptable income proof includes: latest salary slip, last 6 months' bank statement, or proof of foreign tax payment.

questions_and_answers.question: How to attach files larger than 5MB on a ticket?
questions_and_answers.answer: Files larger than 5MB cannot be directly attached to a ticket. Upload them to cloud storage (like Google Drive) and share the link in your ticket.  Instructions are provided for uploading to Google Drive on Android and desktop.

questions_and_answers.question: How to place an investor grievance complaint at Zerodha?
questions_and_answers.answer: To file a complaint, create a support ticket.  Zerodha will provide a resolution.

questions_and_answers.question: How to attach files while responding to a ticket?
questions_and_answers.answer: **Email:** Open the ticket email, click Reply, and either click Attach files or paste files into the email body.  **Support portal:** Click Track tickets, log in, click My tickets, click Choose files, and click Reply.

questions_and_answers.question: Is it possible to create a ticket after the Zerodha account has been closed?
questions_and_answers.answer: Yes, you can create a ticket without logging into your Zerodha account.  Search for the relevant article on support.zerodha.com, click "Create ticket," select "No" for the login prompt, enter your email address, describe your issue, attach any files (if needed), click "Create Ticket," and verify using the OTP sent to your email.

questions_and_answers.question: How to track complaints or tickets at Zerodha?
questions_and_answers.answer: To track tickets: Go to support.zerodha.com, click Track Tickets, log in with your Zerodha credentials, and click the ticket you want to track. To reopen a ticket, click Reopen Ticket, enter your response, and click Reply. If you don't have a Zerodha account, check your email for updates from [email protected] (reply to reopen). Zerodha sends emails when tickets are created and closed.

questions_and_answers.question: How to check if the POA or DDPI is active or inactive for an account?
questions_and_answers.answer: **Kite app:** Click your Client ID, then Profile.  **Kite web:** Log in to Kite.zerodha.com, click your Client ID, then My Profile.  For online account holders, CDSL TPIN authorizes security debits; you can use DDPI instead of TPIN.

questions_and_answers.question: How to sell shares if POA or DDPI is not submitted?
questions_and_answers.answer: If you haven't submitted a POA or DDPI, you can sell holdings using a CDSL TPIN.

questions_and_answers.question: How to revoke the Power Of Attorney (POA) and Demat Debit and Pledge Instruction (DDPI) mapped to Zerodha?
questions_and_answers.answer: **Online (Aadhaar-linked mobile number):** Print the Revocation of Power of Attorney-DDPI form (PDF), fill it out, sign it, scan it, e-sign it, and submit it via a support ticket.  **Offline (non-individual accounts, joint accounts, or no Aadhaar-linked mobile number):** Print the Revocation of Power of Attorney-DDPI form (PDF), fill it out, sign it, and courier it to Zerodha's Bengaluru address. Revocation takes up to 5 business days. After revocation, use CDSL T-PIN to sell shares.

questions_and_answers.question: How to avoid CDSL TPIN and OTP while selling securities in Zerodha?
questions_and_answers.answer: To avoid using CDSL TPIN and OTP for every sale, submit a Demat Debit and Pledge Instruction (DDPI).  This document authorizes your broker to debit securities from your account and deliver them to the exchange.

questions_and_answers.question: How can the Zerodha account be deactivated?
questions_and_answers.answer: To temporarily stop trading, use Kill Switch. For deactivation due to employer restrictions, see "How can Zerodha be empanelled as a registered broker with a company?". Deactivation freezes your demat account (no credits/debits), blocks access to Kite and Console, but maintains AMC and other charges.  You'll still receive statements. Deactivate by downloading, printing, and filling out the Account Closure/Deactivation Form (PDF) and couriering it to Zerodha's Bengaluru address or by e-signing the form and submitting it via a support ticket.  Reactivation involves couriering a reactivation letter (PDF), PAN card copy, and address proof to Zerodha.  If your demat account was closed, you'll need to submit a demat application (PDF).  If the account was closed (not just deactivated), you must reopen it.

questions_and_answers.question: What documents are required to change the company name in a corporate account?
questions_and_answers.answer: To change a corporate demat account's company name, you need: a KYC form (PDF) signed by all authorized signatories/directors with the company seal; a certificate of incorporation showing the new name, signed and sealed; account opening annexures; a request letter; an account modification form (PDF) signed and sealed; a PAN copy showing the new name, signed and sealed; and an MCA certificate, signed and sealed. Email soft copies to [email protected] and courier hard copies to Zerodha's Bengaluru address.  Account updates take up to 72 hours.

questions_and_answers.question: How to update the name while e-signing through Digio?
questions_and_answers.answer: If your Aadhaar name and digital signature name differ, your e-signed forms will be rejected. To update your name in Digio: Click "Change name and Proceed," enter your Aadhaar number, click "Send OTP," enter the OTP, and click "Verify OTP."  Then, continue e-signing. If you don't need to change your name, click "Proceed" to complete the e-signature.

questions_and_answers.question: Why is the error "Nominee addition cannot be processed online for your account. Please initiate request offline." displayed?
questions_and_answers.answer: This error appears for joint accounts, non-individual accounts, and clients without a Zerodha demat account. For joint accounts, all holders must sign the nomination form (PDF) and mail it to Zerodha's Bengaluru address.  Per CDSL guidelines, only individual demat accounts can add nominees online; non-individual accounts cannot.  Clients without a Zerodha demat account also cannot add a nominee.

questions_and_answers.question: Why is the error "DDPI cannot be enabled online for your account. Please initiate request offline." displayed?
questions_and_answers.answer: This error message shows up for NRO accounts, non-individual accounts, and clients without a Zerodha demat account. To activate DDPI, download the DDPI form (PDF), fill it out, and courier it to Zerodha's Bengaluru address. Ensure the signature matches your account's signature. Activation takes up to 72 hours; a confirmation email will be sent.

questions_and_answers.question: Why is the error "Mobile number updation cannot be processed online for your account. Please initiate request offline." displayed?
questions_and_answers.answer: This error message shows up for non-individual account holders and clients who don't have a Zerodha demat account. For instructions on updating your contact details, see "How to change the contact details registered with Zerodha?"

questions_and_answers.question: Why is the error "Email ID updation cannot be processed online for your account. Please initiate request offline." displayed?
questions_and_answers.answer: This error message appears for non-individual account holders and those without a Zerodha demat account. For instructions on how to update your email address, see "How to change the contact details registered with Zerodha?"

questions_and_answers.question: Why is the error "Account closure cannot be processed online for your account. Please initiate request offline." displayed?
questions_and_answers.answer: This error occurs for non-individual account holders and clients without a Zerodha demat account. For account closure instructions, see "What is the process to close a non-individual Zerodha account?"

questions_and_answers.question: Why is the error "Bank account addition cannot be processed online for your account. Please initiate request offline." displayed?
questions_and_answers.answer: This error message appears for NRI clients, minor account holders, and those without a Zerodha demat account. To add a secondary/tertiary bank account, print the Account Modification Form (PDF), fill it out, include bank proof, and courier it to Zerodha's Bengaluru address. Processing takes up to 48 hours; a confirmation email will be sent. There are no charges.

questions_and_answers.question: Why is the error "Primary bank change cannot be processed online for your account. Please initiate request offline." displayed?
questions_and_answers.answer: This error message applies to several account types: individual accounts without Aadhaar-linked mobile numbers or email IDs; individual accounts with proprietorship bank accounts; joint accounts; accounts without a Zerodha demat account; NRE and NRO-PIS accounts; and non-individual accounts. For these accounts, courier the account modification form (PDF) and bank proof to Zerodha's Bengaluru address. Ensure your signature matches your account's. See "Where can the submitted documents be checked while opening an account?".  The change takes up to 72 hours; a confirmation email is sent. There's a ₹25 + GST charge.

questions_and_answers.question: Why is the error "Segments cannot be enabled online for your account. Please initiate request offline." displayed?
questions_and_answers.answer: The error "Segments cannot be enabled online for your account. Please initiate request offline" is displayed for non-individual, NRI, minor account holders and clients who do not have a demat account with Zerodha.

questions_and_answers.question: What is the procedure for changing the registered address of LLP, corporates, trust and partnership firms with Zerodha?
questions_and_answers.answer: To change the registered address, courier the following documents: Non-individual KYC forms (PDF), Account Modification Form (PDF), board resolution (for companies/LLPs), authority letter (for partnerships/trusts), and address proof. Email soft copies to [email protected] for review.  After review, courier the documents to: Zerodha, 153/154, 4th Cross, J.P Nagar 4th Phase, Opp. Clarence Public School, Bengaluru - 560078.  A modification charge of ₹25 + 18% GST will apply, and the update will take 72 working hours.

questions_and_answers.question: What is the procedure for changing the signature at Zerodha?
questions_and_answers.answer: To change your signature, you can either courier the required documents or visit the Zerodha head office.  If couriering, you need an Account Modification Form (PDF), a Banker's letter (PDF), a self-attested copy of your PAN card, and a self-attested copy of your address proof. Email soft copies to [email protected] for review, then courier the documents to Zerodha. If visiting the head office, bring the Account Modification Form (PDF), a self-attested copy of your PAN card, and a self-attested copy of your address proof.  A modification charge of ₹25 + 18% GST applies, and the update takes 72 working hours.

questions_and_answers.question: How can the address registered with Zerodha be changed online?
questions_and_answers.answer: The address can only be changed online if your mobile number is linked to your Aadhaar. Otherwise, use the offline process. To update online: 1. Visit signup.zerodha.com/kite/login and log in. 2. Click "Update details as per Aadhaar". 3. Click "Link your Digilocker with Zerodha" and link it using your Aadhaar, OTP, and 6-digit Digilocker Security PIN. 4. Click "Continue," "Allow," and "Proceed." 5. Fill out the FATCA declaration and click "Continue." 6. Tick the checkboxes and click "Continue." 7. Complete the IPV, and click "Save". 8. Upload a copy of your PAN. 9. Click "e-sign KYC," "Proceed to e-sign," and "Sign now." 10. Tick the checkboxes, enter your Aadhaar number, and verify the OTP. The address will update within 72 working hours; a ₹25 + 18% GST charge applies.  If your Aadhaar name differs from your digital signature, the e-signed forms will be rejected.  NRIs and non-individual account holders must use the offline process.  For minor accounts, use the minor's Aadhaar number (step 3 and 10), and ensure the minor and guardian are visible in the IPV (step 7).

questions_and_answers.question: How to update PAN details on an existing Zerodha account?
questions_and_answers.answer: To update your PAN details, create a ticket with the following e-signed documents: an Account Modification Form (PDF); a self-attested copy of your new PAN card with your signature; a self-attested copy of your address proof; an intimation letter from the Income Tax Department (ITD) for deletion/deactivation of your old PAN; and a handwritten, self-attested letter explaining the reason for the old PAN cancellation, including both old and new PAN numbers.  Alternatively, you can courier these documents to Zerodha. The signature must match your account opening signature. A ₹25 + 18% GST modification charge applies.

questions_and_answers.question: How can F&O segment be deactivated?
questions_and_answers.answer: A segment can be deactivated using Kill Switch.  See "What is Kill Switch?" for instructions.

questions_and_answers.question: How to eSign documents?
questions_and_answers.answer: To eSign documents using Digilocker, your Aadhaar must be linked to a mobile number. There are no charges.  Follow these steps: 1. Log in to digilocker.gov.in. 2. Click "Drive," then "Documents," and "UPLOAD FILE." 3. Upload your document and click "Sign." 4. Enter your Aadhaar number and click "Get OTP." 5. Enter the OTP, tick the consent box, and click "Submit." 6. Download the signed document.

questions_and_answers.question: How to update the income details for the Zerodha account?
questions_and_answers.answer: Zerodha may request income updates due to PMLA surveillance or periodic SEBI reviews for derivatives trading. To update: 1. Visit signup.zerodha.com/rekyc/income. 2. Log in with your Zerodha credentials. 3. Click "Authorize." 4. Select your income slab and optional income proof. 5. Accept the undertaking and click "Continue." The update will be completed within 72 hours, and you will receive an email confirmation.  While submitting income proof is optional, it's required for F&O trading; otherwise, your F&O segment will be disabled.

questions_and_answers.question: How to remove password protection from a PDF document?
questions_and_answers.answer: 1. Enter the password and open the PDF. 2. Click "Menu," then "Print." 3. Select "Print to PDF" and click "Print." 4. Choose a save location, enter a filename, and click "Save".

questions_and_answers.question: What is the procedure for changing the address registered with Zerodha offline?
questions_and_answers.answer: To change your address offline, courier the following to Zerodha: account modification and KYC forms (PDF); a self-attested copy of your PAN card; and a self-attested copy of one of the following address proofs: driving license, voter ID, passport, Aadhaar card (masked), NREA job card, or NPR letter.  A ₹25 + 18% GST modification charge applies.  The address will be updated within 72 working hours.  For NRIs, the address proof must be notarized.

questions_and_answers.question: How to change the name in the Zerodha account?
questions_and_answers.answer:
Zerodha account names are sourced from the Income Tax Department (ITD), so discrepancies may exist.  First, update your name with the ITD. Then, provide the following documents to Zerodha, ensuring the signatures match your account opening signature:

**For Minor Name Changes:** Account modification form and KYC (PDF), Annexure B (PDF), self-attested PAN copy, and self-attested address proof (masked Aadhaar preferred). E-sign these and submit them via a ticket.

questions_and_answers.question: Why was an email with the updated Client Master Report (CMR) sent by Zerodha?
questions_and_answers.answer: Zerodha sends an updated CMR email for the following reasons: a new demat account was opened; account details were modified; the demat account was converted to BSDA or non-BSDA; a demat account was mapped or unmapped from a trading account; or the Zerodha account was closed.  The email includes the CMR link's validity period.  To learn how to obtain a CMR, see "What is Client Master Report (CMR), and how to get it?"

questions_and_answers.question: What is Client Master Report (CMR), and how to get it?
questions_and_answers.answer: A Client Master Report (CMR) is a digitally signed PDF certificate containing your demat account details.  It's used to transfer shares between brokers. To get your CMR: 1. Visit console.zerodha.com/dashboard. 2. Click "Account," then "Documents." 3. Select "Zerodha CMR copy" and click "E-mail to me."  The CMR will be available for download 48 working hours after account opening.

questions_and_answers.question: Where can the DP name be viewed?
questions_and_answers.answer: To view the DP name: 1. Log in to console.zerodha.com. 2. Click "Account," then "Demat."  Zerodha Broking Limited is the Depository Participant (DP) and a CDSL member.  Accounts opened before September 15, 2015, may use IL&FS (DP) with NSDL as the depository; see "How to switch demat account from IL&FS to Zerodha?" for instructions on switching.

questions_and_answers.question: What are DP name, DP ID, BO ID and demat ID?
questions_and_answers.answer: * DP Name: Zerodha Broking Limited (a CDSL member).  * DP ID: 12081600 or 12081601 (or IN300095 for accounts opened before September 15, 2015). * BO ID: Your 8-digit Beneficiary Owner Identification Number, unique to your demat account. * Demat ID: Your 16-digit demat ID (a combination of your DP ID and BO ID), needed for IPO applications and CDSL TPIN generation. To view these IDs: 1. Go to console.zerodha.com/dashboard. 2. Click "Account," then "Demat."  See "How to switch demat account from IL&FS to Zerodha?" for instructions if your account was opened before September 15, 2015.  See "How do I generate the CDSL TPIN required to authorise my CNC sell transactions?" for CDSL TPIN information.

questions_and_answers.question: How to add a nominee to the Zerodha account online?
questions_and_answers.answer: To add a nominee online, your mobile number must be linked to your Aadhaar.  Here's how: 1. Log in to console.zerodha.com. 2. Click "Account," then "Nominees," then "Add nominee."  (Up to 3 nominees can be added; specify the percentage share for each.) 3. Enter nominee details. 4. Click "Continue," agree to the terms and conditions, and click "Proceed." 5. Click "Sign now," accept the terms, enter your Aadhaar number, and click "Send OTP." 6. Enter the OTP and click "Verify OTP." You'll receive an email confirmation; the nominee will be added within 5 business days. If your mobile number isn't linked to Aadhaar, use the offline process. If you encounter an "Invalid Pincode" error, see "Why is the Invalid Pincode error displayed while adding a nominee online?". Nominee names must match their documents; non-individual accounts cannot have nominees; for minors, provide guardian details; the guardian cannot be the nominee for minor accounts; the nomination applies to trading, demat, and Coin mutual fund accounts; dormant accounts must be reactivated first; joint account holders must use the offline method; NRIs can use this method if their Aadhaar is linked to their mobile number; and charitable trusts cannot be nominees.

questions_and_answers.question: Why is the error "Invalid Pincode" displayed while adding a nominee online?
questions_and_answers.answer: Zerodha uses the pincodes available on the Indian Post website to avoid exchange rejections. The "Invalid pincode" error is displayed when the pincode entered is unavailable on the Indian Post website. If the pincode is linked to a different city, that city name is fetched and displayed. To check the pincodes updated on the Indian Post website, visit indiapost.gov.in/vas/pages/LocatePostOffices.aspx.  Zerodha does not send any postal communication to the nominees. Clients can choose a pincode of a neighbouring post office.

questions_and_answers.question: What is the inactivity alert?
questions_and_answers.answer: When there has been no trading activity for 12 consecutive months, exchanges consider the account dormant and deactivate it. The account can be reactivated by verifying the KYC details. If the reactivation is not done within 30 days, Zerodha will alert the nominee(s). This is done to notify the nominee(s) of the Zerodha account.

questions_and_answers.question: How to add a nominee(s) to the Zerodha account offline?
questions_and_answers.answer: To add a nominee(s) to the Zerodha account offline, courier the nomination form (PDF) to: Zerodha, 153/154, 4th Cross, J.P Nagar 4th Phase, Opp. Clarence Public School, Bengaluru - 560078. If an additional nominee needs to be added, the account modification form (PDF) and the nominee form (PDF) must be sent.  The nominees' names must match their documents. An email notification is sent to the nominee if the account holder hasn't completed Re-KYC within 30 days or if the account has been inactive for 12 consecutive months. Non-individual accounts cannot have a nominee. If the nominee is a minor, mention guardian details and ID proof. The account holder cannot be the guardian. For minor accounts, the guardian cannot be the nominee. The nominee applies to the trading and demat account, including mutual fund investments through Coin. Dormant account holders must reactivate the account first. Charitable trusts cannot be added as a nominee. Joint account holders can only add nominees offline. NRIs can add nominees online if their Aadhaar is linked to their active mobile number.

questions_and_answers.question: How to update or modify the nominee details in Zerodha?
questions_and_answers.answer: A nominee can be added online if the mobile number is linked to Aadhaar and a nominee wasn't added earlier.  Online: Only the following existing nominee details can be modified online: Date of birth, Address (requires ID proof, masked Aadhaar preferred), Relationship, Email ID, Mobile number. To modify, create a ticket with the nominee form (PDF) and e-signed account modification form (PDF). The nominee cannot be changed or deleted online. Offline: To change the nominee or modify details, courier the signed nominee form (PDF) and account modification form (PDF). To delete a nominee, courier the signed account modification form (PDF) and annexure 1B (PDF). Courier forms to: Zerodha, 153/154, 4th Cross, J.P Nagar 4th Phase, Opp. Clarence Public School, Bengaluru - 560078.  Updates take 5 working days. An account modification fee applies.

questions_and_answers.question: Can an NRI be added as a nominee to a resident Zerodha account?
questions_and_answers.answer: Yes, an NRI can be added as a nominee to a resident Zerodha account. The NRI's address and mobile number must be Indian. Address proof is not required.

questions_and_answers.question: How to verify the nominee(s) details associated with a Zerodha account?
questions_and_answers.answer: To verify nominee details, log in to console.zerodha.com, click on "Account," then "Nominees."  Nominee details can also be verified on the CMR copy.

questions_and_answers.question: Why has the exchange or depository sent an email asking to add a nominee to the Zerodha account?
questions_and_answers.answer: Per SEBI circular, exchanges and depositories must ask clients to opt in or out of a nomination.  No action is required from the client as Zerodha has communicated their preferences, and the trading account will remain unaffected. Zerodha recommends adding a nominee for seamless succession.  Clients who don't wish to add a nominee can ignore the email.

questions_and_answers.question: How to transfer shares from other brokers to Zerodha?
questions_and_answers.answer: Shares can be transferred via closure cum transfer (free, account closure required) or off-market transfer (fee may apply, account remains open).  Closure cum transfer:  Online or offline. Offline requires forms from the existing broker, a signed Zerodha CMR, and submission to the existing broker.  Securities under lock-in cannot be transferred between depositories (CDSL/NSDL) but can be transferred within the same depository. Off-market transfer: Use CDSL Easiest (online, if supported by broker) or Delivery Instruction Slip (DIS). CDSL Easiest: Register on CDSL, log in to web.cdslindia.com, set up bulk transfer, enter details (BOID, ISINs, quantity, reason), pay stamp duty if needed, submit, verify, commit, and enter OTP.  DIS: Obtain DIS from the broker, fill with Zerodha demat details, submit to the broker.  Transferred shares appear in Kite and Console holdings; buy average price needs manual update.

questions_and_answers.question: How to transfer shares from a Zerodha demat account to another demat account offline?
questions_and_answers.answer: To transfer shares offline, submit the Delivery Instruction Slip (DIS) to Zerodha.  The receiver must be added as a beneficiary on CDSL.  Use the DIS Annexure form for more than 5 securities. If the receiver isn't a beneficiary, include Annexure A.  Zerodha verifies the transfer via call or email; video verification is needed for transfers over ₹5 lakhs.  For off-market sales, include transferee's payment bank details and the applicable stamp duty.  Charges are 0.03% of turnover or ₹25 per ISIN, whichever is higher, + 18% GST. Don't sell shares before approval. Ensure sufficient funds.  Provide NSDL CMR if self-transferring to an NSDL account. Countersign any corrections.

questions_and_answers.question: Can shares be transferred to minors?
questions_and_answers.answer: Yes, shares, ETFs, and gold bonds can be transferred from a guardian's account to a minor's account using Zerodha's gifting feature or CDSL Easiest.

questions_and_answers.question: How to transfer government securities (G-secs) or Sovereign Gold Bond Scheme (SGB) from Zerodha to RBI retail direct account?
questions_and_answers.answer: Government securities and gold bonds can only be transferred via a value-free transfer. Rematerialisation charges apply.  1. Send these documents to Zerodha:  Rematerialisation request form (PDF) for each G-sec or SGB, Value-free transfer letter (PDF) for each G-sec or SGB, Screenshot of RDG account profile, Self-attested PAN. Courier to Zerodha.  Zerodha will provide a Rematerialisation Request Number (RRN). 2. On the RDG account (rbiretaildirect.in), go to Investor Services > Request. Enter ISIN, quantity, Source Depository (CDSL), Depository Participant Name (Zerodha Broking Limited), DP ID, BO ID, a reference number, and upload the RRN. Submit.  The transfer takes up to 3 weeks. Transfers from RBI to demat are not allowed.

questions_and_answers.question: What are the different ways to transfer shares from a Zerodha demat account to another demat account?
questions_and_answers.answer: Shares can be transferred online or offline. Online methods include using CDSL Easiest (for CDSL or NSDL recipient accounts) or gifting (if the recipient has a Zerodha account). Offline methods involve submitting a Delivery Instruction Slip (DIS).

questions_and_answers.question: How to transfer shares from one Zerodha account to another Zerodha account?
questions_and_answers.answer: Shares can be transferred online (as gifts or using CDSL Easiest) or offline (using a Delivery Instruction Slip (DIS)).

questions_and_answers.question: What is the process for an inter-depository SGB, G-sec and SDL transfer?
questions_and_answers.answer: Inter-depository SGB transfers (NSDL to CDSL or vice-versa) require rematerialization and dematerialization requests submitted simultaneously.  To transfer from NSDL to CDSL (Zerodha): Submit rematerialization request to NSDL DP.  Submit dematerialization request to CDSL DP (Zerodha). Courier to Zerodha. To transfer from CDSL (Zerodha) to NSDL: Submit rematerialization request to CDSL DP (Zerodha). Submit dematerialization request to NSDL DP. The process takes up to 3 weeks; charges apply.

questions_and_answers.question: How to transfer shares from the Zerodha account to other CDSL demat account using CDSL Easiest?
questions_and_answers.answer: As per CDSL's circular, to prevent incorrect transfers, all off-market transfers will be processed only if the sender adds the receiver's demat account as a beneficiary on CDSL. To transfer securities from the Zerodha account using CDSL Easiest, follow these steps: 1. Register on CDSL. 2. Log in to web.cdslindia.com/myeasitoken/home/login and click on Setup under Transactions. 3. Click on Bulk Setup. 4. Click on Transaction and enter the execution date and enter the Beneficiary owner ID (BOID) of the person to whom the securities are to be transferred. 5. Click on Account ISINs and select the ISINs in the holdings from the list. Enter the quantity and select the reason for the trade. If the off-market transfer is not a gift or self-transfer and involves a consideration, stamp duty must be paid to CDSL online before making the transfer. 6. Click on Submit. 7. Click on Verify. 8. Click on Commit and then enter the OTP received on the registered mobile number and email. 9. Enter the 8-digit alphanumeric CDSL easiest PIN received on the registered email ID. Do not enter the 6-digit CDSL TPIN. First-time users must change the default PIN. If the PIN was not received or forgotten, visit web.cdslindia.com/myeasitoken/home/login , click on Miscellaneous and then on Reset PIN. This is now sent to the Depository Participant (DP) for confirmation. The request is approved on confirmation, and the transfer will be done.

questions_and_answers.question: How to transfer shares from Zerodha to NSDL demat account via CDSL Easiest?
questions_and_answers.answer: To transfer shares from Zerodha to NSDL demat account via CDSL Easiest, follow these steps: 1. Register for CDSL easiest as a Trusted account. 2. Purchase an e-token from the e-token vendors. 3. Fill up the Request of Authorisation Form (RA form) (PDF) and print out the screenshots of the e-token certificate. 4. A confirmation email is sent once Zerodha has received the forms and the e-token certificates via courier. Once the confirmation is received, clients must change the mode of operations from Trusted to Account Of Choice. 5. Once the above process is completed, clients must create a ticket of the RA form, a screenshot of the e-token certificate on Internet Explorer, and a screenshot of the E-Token registration on CDSL before couriering them to: Zerodha, 153/154, 4th Cross, J.P Nagar 4th Phase, Opp. Clarence Public School, Bengaluru - 560078 5. Once the above process is completed, the e-token will be mapped by CDSL within 20 working days. After the e-token is mapped, shares can be transferred online. To learn more, see How to transfer shares from the Zerodha account using CDSL Easiest?

questions_and_answers.question: How to accept gifted securities?
questions_and_answers.answer: A Zerodha account is required to accept the gifted stocks. An email and SMS with the details of the gifted securities are sent to the receiver. To accept gifted securities, follow these steps: Click on the link received in the email or SMS. Login using the Zerodha credentials. Click on Accept gift. Once the receiver accepts the gift, the sender must authorise the transfer using CDSL TPIN. The stocks are then transferred to the receiver’s account and are displayed under holdings.

questions_and_answers.question: What are the charges for gifting stocks?
questions_and_answers.answer: The standard off-market transfer fee of ₹25, or 0.03% per stock, whichever is higher + 18% GST, is applicable. There are no additional charges for gifting securities.

questions_and_answers.question: Why are the gifted securities not visible under holdings?
questions_and_answers.answer: Gifted stocks may not be visible in the holdings for the following reasons: The sender of the gift has not completed the CDSL OTP verification; The sender has completed the CDSL OTP verification after the cut-off time of 8 PM; The sender is trying to gift stocks during lock-in or freeze.

questions_and_answers.question: Are there any income tax implications on the gifting of shares?
questions_and_answers.answer: A gift may be in the form of money, immovable or movable property. Understanding the tax implications and disclosure in Income Tax returns and maintaining documentation is important. To learn more about taxes, visit learn.quicko.com/tax-gifted-shares-securities. Tax implications in the hands of the sender of the gift¹: The sender of the gift is not liable to pay taxes as the Gift Tax Act (GTA) was abolished. According to the Income Tax Act, capital gains can arise from the transfer of a capital asset. However, gift is expressly excluded from the definition of transfer under Section 47. Therefore, income tax on such a transaction is not liable to be paid by the sender of a gift. Tax implications in the hands of the receiver of the gift: Under Section 56(2) of the Income Tax Act, the recipient is liable to be taxed for gifts of movable property, such as shares, ETFs, mutual funds, jewellery, drawings, etc., without consideration and exceeding the fair market value of more than ₹50,000. Income from such gifts should be reported under the head Income from Other Sources in the Income Tax Return, and tax at slab rates should be paid. Taxes on the gifting of shares are exempt in the following situations: Individuals receiving gifts from a relative (including siblings, spouse and lineal ascendants or descendants). To learn more, visit learn.quicko.com/gift-under-income-tax-act#exempt. Individuals receive gifts on the occasion of marriage. Gift received by inheritance. On the sale of the gift: If shares, ETFs, mutual funds, etc., are received as a gift and subsequently sold, the income would be taxable under the head Income from Capital Gains. Tax at applicable rates should be paid, and the recipient should file ITR-2. To learn more, visit learn.quicko.com/tax-gifted-shares-securities and learn.quicko.com/equity-share-trading-income-tax-treatment. The holding period for determining the nature of Capital Gains, whether STCG or LTCG, would be determined from the date of acquisition by the previous owner until the date of sale. The capital asset acquisition cost would be determined as the previous owner's purchase price to compute the capital gains. To justify the genuineness of the gift transaction, proper documentation, such as a gift deed, should be maintained by the sender and recipient. In case of high gift amounts, there are chances of scrutiny from the tax department. Notes ¹At Zerodha, for tracking and reporting purposes, the stock's closing price on the day the stock gets transferred is the exit price for the person gifting the stock, and the same price is used as an entry price for the person receiving the gift. The average price is updated within 3 working days after the stocks are transferred. While filing for income tax, a different view can be taken on the acquisition price.

questions_and_answers.question: Why is the buy average price not updated for stocks received as gifts through Console?
questions_and_answers.answer: The buy average price and P&L on Kite and Console will be updated in 3 working days. If the buy average price is not updated after 3 working days, create a ticket. To learn about tax implications when gifting stocks, see Are there any income tax implications on the gifting of shares?

questions_and_answers.question: How to get a Delivery Instruction Slip (DIS) booklet?
questions_and_answers.answer: The DIS method of transferring securities involves receiving and sending physical copies of the DIS. Instead, CDSL easiest can be used to transfer shares online. A DIS request form (PDF) must be submitted to receive the DIS booklet. The DIS booklet will be couriered within 48 hours of receiving the request. The instructions to fill out the DIS request form are as follows: Client ID: Enter the BO ID. See, What are DP name, DP ID, BO ID and demat ID? Collection instructions: Collected by hand: Select this if the client visits the Zerodha head office to collect the DIS booklet. A self-attested copy of the ID proof and the DIS request form must be submitted. Additional Booklet: This option should be selected if a client who has lost Annexure B attached to the existing DIS booklet needs an additional booklet. However, if the client has Annexure B, selecting this option is unnecessary, and the additional booklet can be obtained by sending Annexure B to the head office. Not required to cancel unused slips: This option should be selected if the existing DIS slips are not to be cancelled. In such a case, create a ticket to confirm. Required to cancel unused slips: This option should be selected if the existing DIS slips are to be cancelled. The client needs to mention the slip number and tick any one of the options, i.e., Lost, Misplaced, or Others (the reason should be mentioned if Others is selected). To Cancel DIS slips/book: This option should be selected to cancel the DIS slips without requiring extra booklets. By Authorized Representative: This option must be selected if a representative visits the head office instead of the account holder(s) to collect the DIS booklet. In such a case, the authorised representative must submit the DIS request form and the ID proof, both signed by all the account holder(s). This also applies to non-individual account holders. Clients must ensure the account is not dormant when the representative visits Zerodha. If it is, a call verification/In-Person Verification (IPV) will be conducted with the client to authenticate the representative. Correspondence address: This option must be selected if a client is applying for a new DIS booklet and wants it delivered to their address by Zerodha. DIS booklet will only be sent to the account holder's communication address registered with Zerodha. Name and signatures of all the account holders. The DIS request form can be submitted online and offline: Online The DIS request form can be submitted online by individual account holders if their Aadhaar is linked to a mobile number. To submit the request form, follow these steps: Print the DIS request form (PDF). Fill out the details and sign. Scan the form and eSign. To learn how to eSign, see How to eSign documents? Create a ticket and attach the e-signed DIS request form, which is vertically aligned. The esigned forms must be submitted within 30 days from the date of eSign. Offline If the account holder's Aadhaar is not linked with a mobile number or the client is a non-individual account holder, the offline method must be followed. If the DIS booklet is being requested for the first time, enter the DP ID on the DIS request form (PDF) and courier it. To learn about DP ID, see What are DP name, DP ID, BO ID and demat ID? If an additional DIS booklet is being requested, fill out Annexure B, available on the last page of the existing DIS booklet and courier it. Courier all the documents to: Zerodha, 153/154, 4th Cross, J.P Nagar 4th Phase, Opp. Clarence Public School, Bengaluru - 560078

questions_and_answers.question: How to fill a Delivery Instruction Slip (DIS)?
questions_and_answers.answer: As per CDSL's circular, to prevent incorrect transfers, all off-market transfers will be processed only if the sender (transferor) of the securities adds the receiver's (transferee’s) demat account as a beneficiary on CDSL. To learn how to add a beneficiary on CDSL, see How to add a beneficiary on CDSL to transfer securities? To fill out the Delivery Instruction Slip, follow these instructions: First/Sole Holder’s Name: Enter the account holder's name as mentioned in the demat account. ISIN: Enter the ISIN of securities to be transferred as per the transaction statement. To find the transaction statement, see How to download transaction cum holding (SOT and SOH) statement? *A maximum of 5 securities (ISINs) can be transferred per DIS. Use the DIS Annexure form (PDF) to transfer more than 5 securities. *To transfer securities to multiple accounts, use separate DIS for each account. Security Name: Name of security to be transferred. Quantity in Figures: Enter the quantity in numbers. Quantity in Words: Enter the quantity in words. To be left blank. No of Annexures (if any): Enter the number of DIS Annexures (PDF) attached to the slip if more than 5 securities are transferred. Select the transfer reason. If the reason is selected as Others, enter the reason mentioned in the list (PDF). Bank details if it is an off-market sale of a security. The field can be left blank if it is not an off-market sale. Off-Market Trade: While making an off-market transfer, enter the counter DP details, i.e., the DP details to whom the securities are being transferred. *Tick the depository option, CDSL or NSDL. *Counter DP ID, Client ID details, and BO name (account holder's name). *Tick the settlement details as BO-BO. If the securities that are being transferred are not listed or do not trade on the exchanges, leave the field blank. To be left blank. Zerodha will fill in the date after the DIS is executed. Signature box: The account holder's signature must be as per the signature recorded in the Zerodha demat account. Add a counter signature if there are any corrections or an overwritten signature. To check the signature as per Zerodha records, see Where can the submitted documents be checked while opening an account? Charges Transfer charges of 0.03% of turnover or ₹25 per ISIN, whichever is higher, plus 18% GST is applicable. Off-market sale To make an off-market sale, follow these steps: Submit the filled DIS slip. Fill in the details of the transferee's payment bank (the person receiving the shares) in the slip. If the DIS booklet was issued before Feb 2021, fill in the payment bank details in the Annexure for the DIS slip (PDF) and submit it with DIS. Stamp duty is applicable per the slab mentioned in this document (PDF).

questions_and_answers.question: Can the applicant's representative collect the Delivery Instruction Slips (DIS)?
questions_and_answers.answer: Yes, the applicant's representative can collect the DIS booklet from the following address: Zerodha, 153/154, 4th Cross, J.P Nagar 4th Phase, Opp. Clarence Public School, Bengaluru - 560078 For a fresh DIS booklet, the authorised representative must submit the DIS request form (PDF) and the ID proof, both signed by all the account holder(s). For an additional DIS booklet, the representative must submit Annexure B, which can be found on the last page of the DIS booklet. See How to get a Delivery Instruction Slip (DIS) booklet?

questions_and_answers.question: Can a Delivery Instruction Slip (DIS) be submitted and executed at a Zerodha branch office?
questions_and_answers.answer: No, a Delivery Instruction Slip (DIS) cannot be submitted at a Zerodha branch office. The DIS, along with a hard copy of the Client Master Report (CMR) from the other broker, must be couriered to Zerodha's head office at the following address: Zerodha, 153/154, 4th Cross, J.P Nagar 4th Phase, Opp. Clarence Public School, Bengaluru - 560078 To learn what a CMR is, see What is Client Master Report (CMR), and how to get it?

questions_and_answers.question: How to download transaction cum holding (SOT and SOH) statement?
questions_and_answers.answer: All types of accounts, such as individual, joint, NRI, and non-individual account holders, can download the transaction cum holding statement from CDSL Easi. To learn how to register for CDSL Easi, see What is CDSL Easi and how to register? To download, follow these steps: Login to web.cdslindia.com/myeasitoken/home/login. Click on Transaction and then Transaction cum Holding Statement. Select History Report, enter the date range and click on Submit. Click on Download to download the statement or click on Email to send the statement to the registered email ID. Zerodha also sends the monthly holding statements at the end of every month to the client's registered email ID. It includes all the debit and credit transactions for equity and mutual funds for the month.

questions_and_answers.question: Why was an email from CDSL received stating PAN Verification Reversed?
questions_and_answers.answer: As of June 3rd, 2024, PAN and aadhaar linking is not mandatory (NSE, BSE). Clients can now trade and invest provided all other requisite conditions are met, including having a valid name, PAN, mobile number, email ID, complete address, income details, and KRA compliance. As per the regulations (WEB), trading and investing will be disabled if the PAN is not linked with Aadhaar by 30th June 2023. CDSL will validate if the PAN from the Income Tax Database (ITD) is linked to Aadhaar and send an email if it is not. It can take up to 30 working days for the PAN to be updated in IT records. To learn more, see How to link PAN with Aadhaar? Clients can ignore the email if the PAN is linked to their Aadhaar.

questions_and_answers.question: What is CDSL Easiest?
questions_and_answers.answer: Electronic Access to Securities Information and Execution of Secured Transactions (Easiest) is an internet-based facility offered by CDSL, that allows off-market, on-market, inter-depository, and early pay-in debit instructions to be submitted by Clearing Members of Beneficial Owner (clients) from their demat account. Additionally, a subscriber of Easiest is automatically provided with all the facilities and benefits of Electronic Access to Securities Information (Easi). CDSL Easiest can be used to transfer securities from one demat to another online.

questions_and_answers.question: What is CDSL Easi and how to register for it?
questions_and_answers.answer: CDSL Easi is a portal by Central Depository Services (CDSL) where demat holdings can be viewed, tracked and downloaded. To register for CDSL Easi, follow these steps: Visit web.cdslindia.com/myeasitoken/home/login Under BO ID, enter the 16 digit demat ID. To learn the demat ID, see What are DP name, DP ID, BO ID and demat ID? Under Password, enter PAN along with the date and month of birth and click on Continue. For example, if the PAN number is ALWPG5809L and the DOB is 25-03-1993, enter ALWPG5809L2503. Enter the OTP sent to the registered email ID or mobile number and click on Continue. Enter a username, password, and security question and click on Continue. If multiple demat accounts are held by the same account holder, the demat ID of the accounts can be entered and grouped together. By grouping the demat IDs, multiple demat accounts can be accessed using a single user ID. Click on Continue, and the registration will be successful. To learn how to download statement of holdings (SOH) and statement of transaction (SOT) using CDSL easi, see How to download transaction cum holding (SOT and SOH) statement?

questions_and_answers.question: How to add a beneficiary on CDSL to transfer securities?
questions_and_answers.answer: As per CDSL's circular, to prevent incorrect transfers, all off-market transfers will be processed only if the sender (transferor) of the securities adds the receiver's (transferee’s) demat account as a beneficiary on CDSL. To add a beneficiary on CDSL for off-market transactions, follow these steps: Visit web.cdslindia.com/myeasitoken/Home/Login. Login using Easi or Easiest credentials. If the account isn’t registered, register with Easi or Easiest. To learn more, see What is CDSL Easi and how to register for it? and How to register for CDSL Easiest using the Zerodha demat account? Click on Transaction. Click on BO Linking. Click on BO Linking Setup. Enter buyer’s (receiver’s) BO ID and PAN. To learn how to find the BO ID, see What are DP name, DP ID, BO ID and demat ID? Click on Submit. An email will be sent to the sender to verify the beneficiary details for off-market transactions. To verify the beneficiary details, follow these steps: Click on the link received in the email. Enter seller's (transferor's) PAN and Demat Account No. The demat account number is the 16-digit ID. To learn how to find the demat ID, see What are DP name, DP ID, BO ID and demat ID? Click on Submit. Tick on the beneficiary details and click on Generate OTP. Enter the OTP and click on Accept. Click on OK. The beneficiary is added instantly. Once added, the shares can be transferred using DIS, CDSL Easi/Easiest or Zerodha's gift feature.

questions_and_answers.question: How to register for CDSL Easiest using the Zerodha demat account?
questions_and_answers.answer: The online registration process is applicable only for individual account holders. Non-individual account holders should courier the physical copy of the easiest registration form that is generated once the registration process is completed to Zerodha HO. To register for CDSL Easiest, follow these steps: Visit web.cdslindia.com/myeasitoken/home/login. Demat details: Enter the 8-digit DP ID followed by the 8-digit demat client ID or BO ID and click on Continue. To know the DP ID and the BO ID login to console.zerodha.com/account/demat or see What are DP name, DP ID, BO ID and demat ID? OTP: Enter OTP received on the registered mobile number or email and click on Continue. Account details: In the account details section, enter the preferred username, answer the security question, select the Trusted Account checkbox and click on Continue. There are two Account type: Trusted account transfer: Trusted accounts are those demat accounts where a client wants to transfer their securities through easiest. Trusted account transfer permits the transfer of securities from one client to another. Account holders (Beneficiary Owners) can transfer the securities to four CDSL demat accounts of their own choice, which have been added as trusted accounts. Transactions through the trusted account option can be set up and have to be approved by an additional PIN, which will be emailed to the BO separately. If the BO opts for the trusted account option, they will receive two separate emails with two separate passwords, one for accessing the easiest log-in and the second for the PIN for authorizing their transactions. To learn more, See How to add a trusted account on CDSL Easiest? Transfers can be done only within the depository (CDSL to CDSL). Account of choice transfer: Account of choice transfer permits the transfer of securities from one account holder (BO) account to another demat account. Transactions are authenticated through a Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) (e-token), which the BO has to obtain from any of the Registered Authority (RA). The BO will have to submit the easiest registration form signed by all the holders (not applicable for sole holders) and the other Registering Authority (RA) form for mapping the digital signature (e-token) to the DP for authentication. Transfers can be done across the depositories i.e, CDSL to CDSL and CDSL to NSDL. 5. Finish: The registration is complete, and after Zerodha authenticates it, CDSL easiest will be activated for the BO ID. The activation takes up to 48 working hours.

questions_and_answers.question: How to add a trusted account on CDSL Easiest?
questions_and_answers.answer: Stocks can be transferred from CDSL Easiest only to a trusted demat account. To register with CDSL easiest and add a trusted account during registration, See How to register for CDSL Easiest using the Zerodha demat account? Up to 4 trusted accounts can be mapped at a time. If a new account needs to be added, an existing account that is mapped has to be deleted. Deletion requests are approved within 24 working hours. The below process can only be followed to add CDSL demat accounts as trusted accounts. To transfer shares to an NSDL account, see How to transfer shares from Zerodha to NSDL demat account via CDSL Easiest? To add a trusted account on CDSL Easiest, follow these steps: Log in to web.cdslindia.com/myeasitoken/home/login. Click on Miscellaneous and then Edit Trusted Account. Click on Add Trusted Account and enter the 16-Digit CDSL BO ID where stocks must be transferred. If the trusted account is a Zerodha account, the BO ID can be viewed on Console, see What are DP name, DP ID, BO ID and demat ID? Securities, once transferred to the incorrect BO ID, cannot be reversed, similar to a fund transfer to a wrong bank The trusted account will be approved within 24 working hours, after which the stocks can be transferred.

questions_and_answers.question: Why did CDSL send an email with the transaction details?

Enter the new password. Click on Submit. 1 If the login name is unknown, follow these steps: Visit the CDSL forgot username page. Enter BO ID. To learn more about BO ID, see What are DP name, DP ID, BO ID and demat ID? Enter the PAN. Click on Submit. Enter the OTP sent to the mobile number and email ID. Click on Submit.

questions_and_answers.question: Why was an email received from CDSL stating UCC is delinked from the demat account?
questions_and_answers.answer: A circular issued by SEBI that mandates the mapping of a client's Unique Client Code (UCC), with which they open an account with a broker, and their demat account number (BO ID) is the reason behind the email. The purpose of this requirement is to establish systematic checks. To learn more about client code and BO ID, see What is the user ID to log in to Zerodha’s trading platform? And What are DP name, DP ID, BO ID and demat ID? The mapping enables regulators to ensure that shares sold by a client are debited from their account and shares purchased by the client are credited to their account. The mapping occurs between the UCC, demat account, trading member ID (broker ID), clearing member ID, and account segments. Therefore, if a Zerodha trading and demat account is opened, the mapping occurs on the back-end (backend of exchange {NSE and BSE} + depository {CDSL} clearing corporation {NCL}). The Zerodha Client ID is mapped with the following: Zerodha demat account number. Zerodha's trading member ID with the exchange. Zerodha's clearing member ID with the clearing corporation. Segments that are enabled in the account (NSE, BSE, NFO, CDS, etc.). All client IDs with different brokers get mapped to all the demat accounts that have been opened. If a client has multiple trading accounts with different brokers, their demat account at Zerodha will be mapped to all the unique client codes. For example, if a client has 5 trading accounts (including Zerodha) with 5 stockbrokers, the demat account at Zerodha will be mapped to 5 different Unique Client Codes. The mapping between the UCC and the demat account changes based on the status of the UCC. If a broker changes the status of the UCC from Active to Inactive or Closed, the UCC to demat linking gets unmapped or de-linked. In this case, one of the other brokers that the client has an account with has changed the status of their client ID from Active to Inactive at their end, resulting in the delinking of the UCC from the Zerodha demat account. CDSL sends an email to notify the client of the same. The changes made by CDSL will not affect the trading activity with Zerodha, and the email can be ignored. CDSL will inform the client of the changes made to their system the next day. In the email, V stands for Verified and D for Delinked.
