What is Console?: Console (WEB), provided by Zerodha, is an online back-office platform that grants clients access to a wide range of account-related information, reports, statements, and analytics. Through Console, users can access and download reports, analyze performance metrics, and manage funds.
What are the different ways of transferr: This question's answer is not directly provided in the given text; the previous answer mentions that funds must be transferred manually if an eMandate transaction fails.
What is a quarterly settlement or runnin: As per SEBI’s circular (WEB), funds in the trading account must be transferred back to the client's bank account once a quarter. At Zerodha, settlement happens on the first Friday of the quarter. However, funds are transferred back to the primary bank account once a month if the client is inactive for 30 calendar days. Brokers may retain the funds if a client has an outstanding position on the first Friday of the quarter and send out an email with the retention statement. If the account is opened after the previous quarterly settlement date, the funds will not be transferred back for the current quarter. If the settlement of funds with a broker is monthly, the settlement date will be the first Friday of the month.
What is a Retention statement?: This question's answer is not directly provided in the given text; the provided text refers to learning more about retention statements.
What is Kill Switch?: The Kill Switch feature can be used to disable a specific trading segment or to take a break from trading. To disable a segment on Kite app: Tap on the user ID, tap on Profile, tap on Segments, tap on the toggle button for the particular segment and then on Continue. The segment will be deactivated within 5 minutes. To enable a segment: Click on the toggle switch for the particular segment and then Continue, select E-mail or Mobile to receive the OTP and click on Continue, enter the OTP and click on Verify. Once a segment is disabled, it can be re-enabled only after 12 hours.
What happens to GTT, basket orders and S: Once the GTT is triggered, if the segment is disabled, the orders are rejected. The same applies to basket orders and SIPs that get triggered.
How to avail Loan Against Securities(LAS: To avail loan against securities from a different NBFC offline, follow these steps: Open a loan against securities account in one of the financial institutions; Once the account is set up, download, print and fill the pledge request form (PDF); Send it to Zerodha. Alternatively, the forms can be esigned and sent to Zerodha by raising a ticket. Non-individual account holders need to follow the offline process. Securities can be unpledged by requesting the financial institution (pledgee). Once the financial entity confirms that there are no dues, they will un-pledge the securities. Alternatively, unpledge request form (PDF) can be filled and submitted offline.
Why is a CKYC error being displayed whil: This error is displayed if there is a discrepancy in the records of PAN, Aadhaar, email, or mobile number in the Central KYC (CKYC) database.  Please create a ticket, and Zerodha Capital will resolve the issue within five days.
How to contact customer support for NBFC: The Zerodha Capital FAQ page (WEB) contains answers to the majority of the loan against securities queries. To speak to Zerodha's representatives for other queries, please create a ticket, and the response will be received within 48 hours.
How to download contract notes?: The contract notes for the trades are sent to the registered email on the trade date, and the password to open contract notes is the client's PAN in capital letters. To download contract notes: Visit console.zerodha.com/reports/downloads, select Contract note in the statement, select Report type, select a Date range, select Category and Trade type, click on E-mail.  The download link on the email is active for 7 days. Contract notes can only be downloaded for a period of 365 days.
What is the virtual contract note, and h: The virtual contract note provides an approximation of brokerage, STT, stamp duty, exchange transaction charges, SEBI turnover charge, and GST for the day. It also provides order-wise charges, unlike a regular contract note. To view it on the Kite app, tap Orders, then Executed, then Contract note. On Kite web, click Orders, then Contract note.  Note: The virtual contract note does not display the additional brokerage of ₹40 charged when the Zerodha account has a negative balance; DP charges are levied separately on the funds statement; for NRI and Non-individual accounts, the brokerage charge displayed isn't calculated as per the actual rate; and it functions for up to 500 executed orders.  For more than 500, refer to the contract note sent to the registered email.
How to understand the contract note?: A contract note is the legal record of all transactions through stockbrokers on stock exchanges, including all trades executed on a particular day.  They're sent to the registered email on the trade date and can be downloaded from Console. The format changed August 1, 2024.  The first page shows broker and client information, trade date, settlement date, etc. The next page shows segment (equity, derivatives), ISIN, quantities, WAP, and brokerage details.  WAP (Weighted Average Price) is calculated differently for equity and derivatives (formulas provided in the text). The following page displays obligation details: pay-in/pay-out obligations (in brackets if payable, otherwise receivable); applicable brokerages and taxes (GST, STT, stamp duty, SEBI turnover fee, exchange transaction tax) are displayed; and the net amount receivable or payable. Annexure A (on the next page) includes trade details (Order No., Order time, Trade No., Trade time, Security/Contract description, Buy(B)/Sell(S), Exchange, Quantity, Gross Rate/Trade Price Per unit, Brokerage per Unit, Net Rate per unit, Closing Rate per unit (derivatives only), Net total (Before Levies), Remarks). Other charges (call and trade, DP charges) are on the funds statement, not the contract note.  Order and Trade numbers in the format 111111 or 222222 indicate exchange settlement; 333333 indicates physical settlement.  The format of contract notes changed on August 1, 2024; older formats may be displayed for dates prior to this.
Are the F&O positions settled on the exc: Yes.  Open F&O contracts held until expiry and settled on the exchange are displayed. Order no. and Trade no. are displayed as 111111 (options) or 222222 (futures) to indicate exchange settlement; 333333 indicates physical settlement. Order time is 15:40:00, trade time is 00:00:00. The Gross Rate/Trade Price Per unit is the exchange settlement price.
Why is the contract note delayed or not: Contract note delivery may be delayed if the exchanges delay sending trade files to Zerodha.  Generally, they're sent to the client's registered email on the trade date, but processing time depends on when Zerodha receives the files from the exchanges.  Contract notes can also be downloaded from Console.
How to view or download the profit and l: To view or download the P&L report, go to console.zerodha.com/reports/pnl, select the segment, choose Combined, Realised, or Unrealised P&L, select the date range, and click View.  The report can then be downloaded as a spreadsheet.  Note: Zerodha provides no warranty for the authenticity and completeness of the data; clients should cross-check it with their tradebook, contract notes, and funds statement.
How to change the date format of Console: Download the report in CSV format, select the date column, right-click and select Format Cells, click Date, then Custom, and enter the desired format.
How to get the trade and P&L reports for: Trade and P&L reports have been available on Console only since FY 2017-18. To obtain data for earlier periods, create a ticket to request the trade book, contract notes, or ledger.  Clients can manually prepare P&L reports for earlier periods using the trade book and contract notes.
What does the profit and loss heat-map o: The profit and loss heat map on Console visually displays daily gross profit and loss (P&L) reports. Green indicates profit, red indicates loss; lighter shades show smaller amounts, darker shades show larger amounts.  The value displayed when hovering over a tile is the gross realised P&L for that day.
What do 'Other credits & debits' in the: The "Other credits & debits" entry in the Console P&L report refers to charges and credits not directly related to trading activities, excluding brokerage, exchange transaction charges, STT, GST, stamp duty, and SEBI charges (which are on the contract note and funds statement).  This includes call and trade charges, payment gateway charges, DP charges, account opening charges, margin penalty, delayed payment charges, AMC charges, and more.  A breakdown is available in the Tax P&L and the second sheet of the downloaded P&L report.
Why does Kite P&L not match with credit/: Kite (trading platform) and Console (back office) calculate P&L differently, though the overall P&L is consistent. Kite's futures and options position page uses FIFO (First In, First Out) for P&L based on the entry price. Console settles P&L daily using M2M (Marked to Market) for futures positions.  Kite shows overall and current day P&L; Console's ledger shows multiple daily entries, but the overall P&L totals match.
What could be the reason for a profit an: An incorrect P&L report may be due to corporate actions (bonus, splits, rights issues, mergers, spin-offs, buybacks, etc.), discrepant quantities entered for off-market share transfers or IPOs, or short delivery/auction scenarios.  If any of these apply, create a ticket.
How to download the tax P&L or capital g: On Console, click Reports, then Tax P&L, select the financial year and quarter range, click the arrow, and then click "Download Tax P&L report for all segments" at the bottom to download the report.
How to check capital gains applicability: The "View breakdown" option in holdings shows purchase date, quantity, price, age (days since purchase), and P&L.  LTCG (Long-Term Capital Gains) applies to holdings over 365 days; STCG (Short-Term Capital Gains) applies to holdings under 365 days.  To view this information: On the Kite app, tap Portfolio, select the stock, and tap View breakdown. On Kite Web, click Holdings, click Options, and select View breakdown. On Console, click Portfolio, then Holdings, then Options, and select View breakdown/tags.  For more information on market-related taxation, visit zerodha.com/varsity/module/markets-and-taxation.
How is turnover calculated in Tax P&L an: Zerodha uses the turnover calculation on Console to determine if a tax audit is needed, following the guidance note on tax audit under section 44AB.  Turnover is calculated as follows: Delivery: sell-side value; Intraday: absolute sum of profits and losses per stock; F&O (equity, currency, commodity): absolute sum of profits and losses per contract. Note: There may be differences in turnover calculations between the tradewise and segments sheets on the downloaded Tax P&L report; use the tradewise turnover for tax filing.
How are the dividends on Liquid ETFs and: Dividends on Liquid ETFs and Liquid BeES are taxed at the investor's income tax slab rate.  When sold, the dividend value is the cost of acquisition, and any gains are taxed under capital gains (STCG if sold within 3 years, taxed at slab rates; LTCG if held over 3 years, taxed at 12.5% with the first ₹1,25,000 exempt). For purchases after April 1, 2023, all gains are short-term and taxed at the investor's slab rate.  If dividends exceed ₹5,000, an additional 10% TDS applies.  Consult a chartered accountant for tax filing assistance.
What are Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG): Capital gains are profits from selling assets (stocks, bonds, real estate, etc.), the difference between selling and purchase prices.  LTCG (Long-Term Capital Gains) applies to assets held for a specified period (usually over 1 year).  Before July 23rd, 2024, LTCG on securities was taxed at 10%; after that date, it's 12.5%. The LTCG exemption limit is ₹1,25,000 per year (from FY 2024-25). A grandfathering clause allows using the asset's January 31, 2018 price for LTCG calculations for some assets. STCG (Short-Term Capital Gains) applies to assets held for one year or less. Before July 23rd, 2024, STCG on securities was taxed at 15%; after that date, it's 20%.  There's no exemption for STCG.  Specific tax rates for LTCG and STCG vary by asset type and holding period (tables provided in the text).  Download the Tax P&L report for LTCG tax liability.
Who is liable to pay taxes on the P&L in: The primary or first holder of the joint demat account is liable for taxes on the profit and loss.
Why are the returns on liquid ETFs like: Before the 2020 budget, liquid ETFs had a 28.84% Dividend Distribution Tax (DDT), deducted before distributing dividends. Website returns didn't account for this.  After the budget, DDT was removed; dividends are now taxed at the investor's income tax slab rate (plus an additional 10% TDS if dividends exceed ₹5,000).
What should be done when an income tax n: After filing Income Tax Returns (ITR), you may receive a notice (sections 139(9), 143(1), or 143(1)(a)). Contact Quicko (WEB), Zerodha's tax planning and filing partner, for guidance on handling such notices.
How to view the long-term and short-term: Console's "Tags" feature allows tagging securities as long-term (held over 1 year) or short-term (held under 1 year).  Use Console filters to view them separately.  See "How to add tags on Zerodha’s Console?" for instructions. Note:  Holdings can't be sold separately; the FIFO (First-In-First-Out) method is used for tax purposes, regardless of how holdings are viewed.  The investor is responsible for indicating short-term or long-term capital gains/losses when filing taxes.
Can input tax credit be claimed on the G: Yes, if the services are used for business purposes (not by a retail investor) and the GST registration is linked to the demat account's PAN. To add your GST number to contract notes and invoices, provide your GST registration certificate by creating a ticket.  See "How to download the GST invoice for the charges posted on the funds statement?" for instructions.
What is tax loss harvesting?: Tax-loss harvesting is selling losing securities to offset capital gains taxes. For example, if you have ₹100,000 in short-term capital gains (taxed at 15%) and ₹60,000 in unrealized losses, selling the losing stocks reduces your taxable gains to ₹40,000, saving you taxes.  While not explicitly disallowed in India, consult a CA before using this strategy, as it may be questioned by tax authorities if the same stock is quickly repurchased.  A tax-loss harvesting report is available at console.zerodha.com/reports/tax-loss-harvesting/eq.  For more information, see zerodha.com/varsity/module/markets-and-taxation/ and zrd.sh/tax-loss-harvesting-22.  Note: Console uses FIFO (First In First Out) for buy average and P&L; selling a stock to harvest losses may also realize long-term capital gains; the first ₹100,000 of long-term gains is tax-free and not considered in the report; and there's no harvesting opportunity if losses exceed profits.
Where can the holding period of investme: The tax liability for long-term stock investments (under the grandfather clause) is in the Tradewise Tax P&L report on Console. This report shows entry and exit dates and holding period information. See "How to download the tax P&L or capital gains statement at Zerodha?" for download instructions.
What does the Trade book heat map on Con: The trade book heat map visually represents the trade book using color-coding to show the number of trades; lighter colors mean fewer trades, darker colors mean more trades.  It helps identify trading/investing patterns to improve strategy.  View it at console.zerodha.com/reports/tradebook; select the segment and duration to update the heat map.  Clicking a tile shows the number and details of trades for that day.
What is an Annual Information Statement: An Annual Information Statement (AIS) is a report on the income tax portal showing all capital market trades, interest, dividends, and corporate action benefits for a financial year.  FAQs are available on the income tax portal (WEB).  It details investments and income from various sources, helping taxpayers verify transactions before filing ITRs. Discrepancies may arise due to the estimated cost of acquisition being based on the best available price (possibly showing closing prices instead of actual transaction prices).  See blog.quicko.com/decoding-the-new-annual-information-statement for more information.
Where can the trades that are taken for: Trades for a specific period are found in the Tradebook on Console. To download it, log in to console.zerodha.com, click Reports, then Tradebook, select the segment and date range, and click the arrow. Download in XLSX or CSV format.  Use the Symbol tab to view trades for individual stocks and the Tags tab to filter by tags.  The Tradebook heatmap also shows trades (see "What does the Trade book heat map on Console represent?"). Note: Equity (external trades) include trades from corporate actions, IPOs, OFS, buybacks, and transfers between brokers; MF (external trades) include NFO trades and transfers between brokers; and Tradebook can only be downloaded for a 365-day period.
How to download the interest statement?: Log in to console.zerodha.com, click Funds, then Interest statement, select the date, click View, and then click Download CSV.
What is the online DIS marker in the tra: The online DIS marker in Console's trade book indicates that a sell trade was settled using online delivery instructions (instead of a physical Delivery Instruction Slip).  Zerodha uses online processes; the online DIS consent allows for online debit instructions.  Trades settled this way are tagged with "online DIS" in the trade book.
What is Verified P&L and how to use it?: Verified P&L on Console lets you publicly share your profit and loss report via a shareable link. To generate a link: On mobile, log in to console.zerodha.com, tap the context menu, Account, then Verified P&L; select display name, image, description, date range, whether to show trades and segments, and click Save; copy the link. On web, log in, click Account, then Verified P&L; follow the same steps and click Enable public page, then copy the link. The link shows Net Realised P&L (after deducting charges), a heatmap, longest profitable streak, and most profitable day.  The report is tamper-proof. Transferred securities aren't included. You can regenerate the link or switch to private mode.  Personal data is not shown. See tradingqna.com/t/fake-pnl-of-live-trading-finfluencers-scam/152081/34 for more information.
Are any physical documents sent by Zerod: Zerodha does not send physical documents unless specifically requested by the client (e.g., requesting physical annual reports via a ticket). Clients may receive physical annual reports from companies whose shares they hold. To switch from physical to digital annual reports, create a ticket.
How to convert Console reports to PDFs?: Open the XLSX or CSV report in Excel or a spreadsheet program. Go to File, then Export, then Create PDF. Select the save location.  This works for Holdings, P&L, Tradebook, Tax P&L, and other reports.
Can Zerodha provide reports in either so: Yes, create a ticket to request softcopies of P&L, Tax P&L, Funds statement, SOT, and SOH reports with a seal and signature.  Charges are ₹50 + 18% GST for up to 10 pages, and ₹5 per additional page + 18% GST. Hard copies have an additional ₹100 + 18% GST courier charge.  P&L, Tax P&L, and Funds statements can be downloaded without a seal and signature from Console (see links provided in text for instructions).  See "What is a statement of transaction (SOT) and how do I interpret the same?" and "What is the statement of holdings (SOH) and how to interpret the same?" for SOT and SOH download instructions.
What is a Statement Of Transaction (SOT): The Statement of Transactions (SOT) is a statement that provides a detailed explanation of the movement of securities in the demat account. Shares or units sold from the demat account reflect as a debit (Dr) entry and shares purchased reflect as a credit (Cr) entry.  Here are all the entries in the SOT: Particulars - Type of transaction - Description: ON-DR / SETTLEMENT-DR - Debit - Debit entry represents the sale or removal of securities from the demat account; ON-CR / SETTLEMENT-CR - Credit - Credit entry represents the purchase or addition of securities to the demat account; OF-CR - Off-market credit - Credit entry of securities purchased other than the secondary market; OF-DR - Off-market debit - Debit entry of securities sold/removed other than the secondary market; CA – Bonus, CA – Listed Bonus - Corporate Action - Credit transaction on bonus issued; CA – Extinguishment - Corporate Action – Extinguishment of Securities - Debit entry for debt securities on maturity; CA-Split - Corporate Action – Stock Split - Entries for shares that have been split; INTDEP-DR - Inter Depository Debit - Debit entry (for shares, MF units removed from the account) between CDSL to NSDL or vice versa; INTDEP-CR - Inter Depository Credit - Credit entry for adding or transfer of shares from a different depository; CA-Lock-in - Corporate Action – Lock-In- Units - The entry states that units in the demat account have been marked for lock-in; CA-Listed Conversion - Corporate Action – Conversion of securities - When one asset class converts to another; CA-Merger DB - Corporate Action – Merger Debits - When a company merges with another company; CA-Listed Merger CR - Corporate Action – Credits of the resulting entity - Post-merger entry when shares of the listed company are credited; CA - Rights Entitlement - Corporate action - credit on rights issue - Series of entries on temporary credit of rights entitlement; MP: Setp/Acpt/Unpledge - Margin Pledge: Setup/Accepted/ Unpledged - Margin pledge set up or accepted or unpledged; EP: IREM/REVL/DR - Early Pay-in: Earmark set-up/ Reversal/Debit - Set up(IREM) or reversal(REVL) of earmarked securities as early pay-in(EP). Debit(DR) of securities towards early pay-in; PLEDGE - Pledged holdings - Securities that are pledged for Margins; CA-Reinvestment of IDCW - Credit - Credit of the weekly dividend issued against the Liquidbees held in demat account.
What is the Statement Of Holdings (SOH)?: The statement of holdings is a summary of all the securities held in the demat account on a particular date and gives a bifurcation based on the status of those securities. The following information is available in the SOH: Sec Type; ISIN; ISIN NAME; Current Balance; Free Balance; Locked In Balance; Pledge Setup Balance; Safekeep Balance; Pledged Balance; Earmarked Balance; Pledgee Balance; Re-pledge Balance.
Why are some holdings in the Statement o: Holdings are categorized under Safekeep balance in the Statement of Holdings (SOH) when a client freezes them in the demat account. After unfreezing, the holdings are moved to the Free balance in the SOH.
How to understand the credit/debit on fu: The fund statement displays various entries related to F&O obligations, margin debits, margin reversals, etc., for F&O trading. The F&O obligation amount includes the payable or receivable marked-to-market (M2M) amount.  If a futures trade is not closed during the day, the settlement amount will be determined by the difference between the trade price and the closing settlement price. In the case of a carried-forward futures position from the previous day that is still being held, the settlement amount will be based on the difference between the previous day's closing price and today's closing price. If a carried-forward futures position from the previous day is squared off, the settlement amount will be determined by the difference between the previous day's closing price and the square-off price.  In the case of short option positions, M2M is not applied as in futures. Each day the position was held will have a separate entry in the funds statement.
Why is the balance in the funds statemen: The Zerodha account balance is displayed as negative for the following reasons: Daily marked-to-market (M2M) losses; Charges; Utilisation of collateral margin.  A brokerage of ₹40 per executed order will be charged if the Zerodha account has a negative balance. Delayed payment charges of 0.05% per day (18% per annum) will be levied on the debit balance.
How to view the bank account details lin: To view the bank account details on Console, follow these steps: Click on Account; Click on Bank. The primary and secondary bank details are displayed on this page.
How to submit the currency declaration f: RBI has mandated traders to compulsorily have an underlying contracted exposure to foreign currency if they want to trade in the currency derivatives segment. If a trader has an exposure greater than $100 million, they will be required to appoint a custodian participant or an authorised dealer. For traders with a smaller exposure, a declaration that they are trading currencies to hedge their contracted exposure will suffice. At Zerodha, when clients activate their currency segment on Console, they will have to submit the RBI declaration. To activate the currency segment: Login to console.zerodha.com, click on Account, click on Segment, click on NSE - Currency Exchange and/or BSE - Currency Exchange, click on Continue, select the income range, click on Choose file and upload an income proof, accept the terms and conditions, choose to receive the OTP and click on Continue, enter the OTP and click on Verify, click on Proceed then on Sign now, enter the Aadhaar number and click on Send OTP, enter the OTP and click on Verify & sign. If the mobile number is not linked to Aadhaar, clients can print and sign the RBI declaration form (PDF) and courier it along with an income proof to Zerodha.
How to vote on shareholder proposals thr: Companies introduce various resolutions that must be approved by shareholders.  Zerodha provides access to CDSL’s e-voting system on Console. Resident individual shareholders can e-vote on Console by following these steps: Click on Account; Click on Demat; Click on Shareholder e-voting; Enter the OTP and click on Verify; Click on e-voting and vote accordingly. NRI's and non-individual account holders can e-vote by visiting evotingindia.com.
How to update the income details for the: Zerodha may request clients to update their income details for the following reasons: As part of the Prevention of Money Laundering (PMLA) surveillance; Periodic review of clients' financial information as per SEBI guidelines. To update the income proof, follow these steps: Visit signup.zerodha.com/rekyc/income, click on Continue with Kite, login with Zerodha credentials, click on Authorize, select Income Slab, select Income Proof (Optional), accept the undertaking, click on Continue. Any one of the following documents can be submitted as income proof: A Bank statement with the bank logo and seal in the name of the Zerodha account holder for the last 6 months with an average balance of more than ₹10,000; Latest salary slip with gross monthly income exceeding ₹15,000; Latest ITR acknowledgement with gross annual income exceeding ₹1,20,000; Latest Form 16 with gross annual income exceeding ₹1,20,000; Certificate of net worth more than ₹10,00,000; Latest statement of demat holdings with current holdings value exceeding ₹10,000.
Why is Zerodha asking for the income pro: Zerodha may request clients to update their income details for the following reasons: As part of the Prevention of Money Laundering (PMLA) surveillance; Periodic review of clients' financial information as per SEBI guidelines; Yearly Update of Income Details for Clients of Special Category (CSC).  Clients are notified through email or Kite to update their income proof. Failure to complete the process could lead to the deactivation of the Zerodha account.
How to add family members to a Zerodha a: To add family members, follow these steps: Kite app: Tap on Portfolio, tap on Family, tap on Link a sub- account, tap on Link a sub-account again and enter their user ID, PAN and mobile number, tap on Continue. The sub-account holder has to authorize the request by tapping on the verification link and login to Console using the sub-account holder's login details. Kite web: Visit kite.zerodha.com/holdings, click on Family, click on Link a sub-account, enter the sub-account’s Kite user ID, PAN, and mobile number and click on Continue. The sub-account holder has to authorize the request by clicking on the verification link and login to Console using the sub-account holder's login details. To analyze portfolios at a family level: Click on Portfolio, click on Holdings, click on Family. A maximum of 10 accounts can be linked. What does delisting mean?: Delisting is the process of removing stocks from the stock exchange. These will not show up on Kite for trading. Investments in delisted stocks should be considered a loss or be written off completely unless a client can find someone to buy the stock through an off-market transaction. To learn more, see What are the different ways to transfer shares from a Zerodha demat account to another demat account? What if a client misses tendering the shares in the delisting window? The clients can still sell the stocks back to the promoters of the company, who are obligated to purchase the stock even if a client misses to tender their shares. This facility is usually available for a period of 1 year from the date of closing of the tender offer. To learn more, create a ticket. Types of delisting Forced delisting : Forced delisting typically happens due to non-compliance with SEBI listing requirements or other legal issues. Voluntary delisting : Voluntarily delisting refers to companies voluntarily delisting themselves from the exchange because of corporate restructuring. To close an account with delisted shares, they must be transferred to a different demat account using DIS or CDSL easiest if the ISIN is active. Delisted shares cannot be gifted. What is the impact of mergers and spin o: Mergers and spin-offs can have various impacts on shares, depending on the specific details of the corporate actions involved. In a merger, where two companies combine to form a single entity, the impact on the shares of each company can vary depending on the terms of the merger. In most cases, shareholders of the acquired company receive shares in the new, combined entity in exchange for their old shares. The value of the new shares will depend on various factors, such as the relative valuations of the two companies, the terms of the exchange ratio, and the overall market conditions at the time of the merger. In a spin-off, a company separates one of its divisions or subsidiaries into a new, independent entity. This can result in shareholders of the original company receiving shares in the newly created company. The value of these new shares will depend on various factors, such as the market conditions, the new company's strength, and the spin-off terms. Overall, the impact of mergers and spin-offs on shares can be complex and depend on various factors, including the specific terms of the corporate actions involved and the overall market conditions at the time.
Why were the shares not eligible for cor: Investors need to hold the shares in their demat accounts on or before the ex-date or record date to be eligible for corporate action benefits. To learn more, see What does record date and ex-date mean? Shares that have not been credited to the demat account by the record date or ex-date will not qualify for corporate action benefits. However, shares bought on or prior to the day before the ex-date/record date will always be credited, except in the following circumstances: Settlement holiday: In case of a settlement holiday on the ex-date/record date, the shares will be credited to the demat account on the next working settlement day. For instance, if the shares are bought on Monday, but Tuesday (the record date) is a settlement holiday, the shares will only be delivered by Wednesday, which means they won't be eligible for any corporate action benefits. Therefore, shares must be purchased at least one trading day before Monday to ensure that they are available in the demat account on the ex-date/record date. Short delivery: When the seller fails to deliver the shares, it is classified as short. In such situations, the exchange generally carries out an auction and delivers the shares to the demat account by T+2 days. Therefore, if shares are purchased on Monday but credited to the demat account on Wednesday or later due to short delivery, they will not be eligible for corporate action benefits since they were not present in the demat account on the ex-date/record date. Did you know? In case shares are purchased on the ex-date/record date, the stock price would have already decreased to account for the corporate action. This indicates that in nearly all instances, there would be no notional for failing to participate in the corporate action.

Entry - Definition: Net settlement for Equity with settlement number: {value} - The amount due to be credited to the client, or has to be debited from the client’s account, for settling equity trades; MF purchase - The amount debited for the purchase of mutual fund units; Buyback Order Placement charge for {symbol} - The charge for buyback order placement; Being OFS order placement - The charge for Offer For Sale order placement; Provisional TDS amount blocked - TDS blocked on the value of equity sell transactions in non-PIS NRI accounts; Provisional TDS amount reversed - Reversal of provisional TDS after confirming capital gains in non-PIS NRI accounts; TDS payable - The amount debited as TDS on the capital gains realised in NRI non-PIS accounts; Call and trade charges - Fee debited for orders placed by calling Zerodha’s dealer terminal; Payment gateway charges - Fee debited for funds deposited to the trading account via the payment gateway; Short margin penalty - Penalty debited for non-maintenance of sufficient margins; Payout done for quarterly settlement - All available funds in the trading account are transferred to the primary bank account; Delayed payment charges - Funds utilised are higher than the available amount in the trading account; Pledge charges for {symbol} - The cost of pledging; Pledge charges for {symbol} on {yyyy-mm-dd} - Pledge charges for LAS; Unpledge charges for {symbol} on {yyyy-mm-dd} - Unpledge charges for Loan Against Securities (LAS); AMC for Demat Account for {yyyy-mm-dd} to {yyyy-mm-dd} - Account Maintenance Charge(AMC) on demat account.

Who is an Authorised Person (AP) and how: According to SEBI (WEB), an Authorised Person (AP) is an individual, firm, LLP, or corporate body appointed by a stockbroker to act on their behalf.  SEBI doesn't register or charge APs; they're approved by the stock exchange (NSE charges ₹5000 per segment + GST).  APs are supervised by the stockbroker and exchange; they can't handle client funds or securities directly. To appoint an AP, a stockbroker submits an application to the exchange.  Eligibility criteria for individuals include Indian citizenship, age 18+, no fraud/dishonesty convictions, good reputation, at least 10th-standard education, and relevant certification.  For non-individuals, all partners/directors must meet individual criteria, the entity's MoA must include securities business, and sufficient infrastructure is required.  Conditions include the stockbroker's responsibility for AP actions, no direct client interaction by the AP, remuneration solely from the stockbroker, and written agreements between the stockbroker and AP. To register as a Zerodha AP: Be an existing Zerodha client; have an organic lead source (no paid advertising or trade inducement); have at least 100 successful referrals via Zerodha's referral program; create a ticket providing contact information, lead source, entity type, and business nature.  You'll receive a response within two business days.

What is Coin?: Coin is a platform for buying mutual funds online directly from asset management companies with no commission.  Assets (mutual funds, stocks, currencies, bonds) are held in your demat account.  Learn more at coin.zerodha.com; the app is available on Android and iOS.
Can non-individual account holders inves: Yes, using NEFT or RTGS. To pay: Click Buy, enter the amount, click Buy now, then Confirm; make the payment via netbanking using the account details shown on Coin. Funds are transferred on a FIFO (First In First Out) basis; excess funds are refunded within T+4 days.  Funds must be from a bank account linked to your Zerodha account; IMPS transfers are rejected; NAV allocation depends on ICCL settlement (up to 24 hours); HDFC netbanking transfers are instant; current accounts can be used; one transfer can cover multiple orders, but not vice versa; and orders are open in BSE StARMF for T+5 days. The account details on Coin are unique: MFDICC006498ABXXXX (MFDICC = ICCL initials, 006498 = Zerodha's member code, ABXXXX = client login).
What are Direct Mutual Funds?: Direct mutual funds let investors buy funds directly from the Asset Management Company (AMC), bypassing distributors and their commissions, resulting in lower costs and potentially higher returns.  An AMC (Asset Management Company) or fund house invests pooled funds into various financial instruments.  A distributor is an intermediary between the investor and the AMC, earning commissions.  Bypassing the distributor in direct plans means you avoid paying these commissions.  See "Why is the NAV for direct mutual funds higher than regular mutual funds?" for more details.
How to pledge mutual fund investments to: Pledging mutual funds is the same as pledging other securities. See "How to pledge securities to get collateral margin?" for instructions.
What are the charges applicable for inve: There are no charges for investing in mutual funds, ETFs, and mutual fund NFOs through Coin. There are also no DP (Depository Participant) charges.  There are no additional Account Maintenance Charges (AMC) for using Coin because investments are held in demat form.
What are the advantages of using Coin?: Coin offers commission-free investing in direct mutual funds (avoiding the commission expense added to regular plans' expense ratios); step-up SIP (Systematic Investment Plan) features; easy SIP management (start, pause, stop, adjust amounts); NAV order tracking and a wide selection of AMCs and funds; a single portfolio view of stocks and mutual funds (easily pledged for loans); consolidated statements for tax deductions; easier claims by dependents in case of death; and the ability to view fund investments and compare mutual funds.  See "What are Direct Mutual Funds?" and "What is step-up SIP, and how can it be set on Coin web?" for more details.
What is the difference between Coin and: Coin mandates automatically transfer funds from your bank account to the BSE StAR MF ICCL account for SIP orders. Console mandates automatically transfer funds from your bank account to your Zerodha account for stock investments, ETF SIPs, etc.  Coin mandates cannot be used for Console transactions, and vice versa.  Both types of mandates can transfer up to ₹1 crore.  See "What is a Mandate and how to create them for SIPs on Coin app?" and "How to set up automatic fund transfers from a bank account to a Zerodha trading account?" for more details.

Dividends are partial payouts of profits; the NAV decreases after payout. Note: IDCW reinvestment schemes are not currently available on Coin.
Is stamp duty applicable for mutual fund: Yes, stamp duty of 0.005% is applicable and adjusted with the units allotted; it's not a separate charge.  For example, a ₹10,000 investment would have a ₹0.50 stamp duty, reducing the investment to ₹9,999.50 and affecting the number of units allotted accordingly. Note: Stamp duty isn't currently displayed under charges on Console but is expected to be available soon.
How long will it take for mutual fund un: For liquid schemes, units are settled by 7 PM on T day and visible on Console by T+1 day. For non-liquid schemes, units are settled by 7 PM on T+1 day and visible on Console by T+2 day.  See "What is the cut-off time for mutual fund transactions on Coin and what is the applicable NAV?" for NAV and cut-off information. Note: There may be late deliveries (see "Why are the newly allotted units shown as NA on the Coin app?").
How to add a nominee for mutual fund hol: Since Coin mutual funds are held in demat form, the nominee for your demat account also applies to your mutual funds; you don't need to add a separate nominee for mutual funds. See "How do I add a nominee online in Zerodha?" for instructions on adding a demat nominee.  Check your nominee details at console.zerodha.com/account/nominee.  Ignore any AMC communication about nomination if a nominee is already added to your demat account.
Why are investments made on Coin not vis: Coin investments are in demat form, while AMC websites only show folio-based investments.  Also, if your mobile number or email isn't updated with the RTA, you won't be able to log in. See "Why are the email id or mobile number registered with the AMC different from Coin?"
Why is the minimum initial investment fo: Coin processes SIPs as lump-sum investments on your chosen SIP dates. AMCs (fund houses) set minimum initial investment amounts (for the first investment) and minimum additional purchase amounts (for subsequent investments).  Coin's minimum SIP amount may be higher than on the AMC site because of the AMC's minimum initial investment requirement.  For example, if the minimum initial investment is ₹5000 and the minimum additional purchase amount is ₹1000, your first SIP investment must be ₹5000 or more, while subsequent investments can be ₹1000 or more.  To avoid this initial investment requirement, use AMC SIPs (set up directly through Coin).  Minimum initial investment amounts vary across AMCs and schemes.
Why are clients unable to log in to the: Coin investments are in demat form and may not be visible on the AMC website (it's at the AMC's discretion whether to show demat investments).  You can check your investments on Coin and on your CDSL demat holding statements (downloadable from CDSL Easi - see "How to download transaction cum holding (SOT and SOH) statement?").  Note: ELSS statements can be downloaded on Coin (see "What are ELSS funds, and how can the ELSS statement be downloaded?").
How to change email ID or mobile number: The email and mobile number registered with the AMC are the same as your Zerodha details, also shared with CDSL (the depository) and the RTA (Registrar and Transfer Agent). To change them, follow the same process as changing your Zerodha details (see "How to change the registered mobile number or email address with Zerodha online?"). Note: RTAs update their database on weekends; your demat account nominee also applies to Coin investments (see "How to add a nominee to the Zerodha account online?").
Why were the funds not automatically deb: Funds may not be debited even if your SIP is linked to a mandate if: There is insufficient opening balance in your bank account on the transaction (T) day (only the T-day opening balance is considered, funds added on T day don't count); or the bank rejected the fund transfer (contact your bank).
What does exit load mean and how to calc: Exit loads are penalties for early redemption of mutual funds.  The exit load is calculated on the NAV (Net Asset Value) at the time of redemption, based on the factsheet's exit load percentage for the purchase month. What is Console?: Console (WEB), provided by Zerodha, is an online back-office platform that grants clients access to a wide range of account-related information, reports, statements, and analytics. Through Console, users can access and download reports, analyze performance metrics, and manage funds.
How to download the GST invoice for the: On Console (WEB), click Reports, then Downloads, select Invoice under the Statement tab, choose the month, year, and company, and click Download.  Note: GST is only applicable to some charges on the funds statement; it does not apply to Delayed payment charges, STT, and Stamp duty.
Why did CDSL or NSDL deposit money to my: CDSL or NSDL may deposit money into your bank account for several reasons: 1) Interest on Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs) - SGBs pay 2.5% annual interest, credited twice yearly; 2) Dividends; 3) Partial entitlement during corporate actions (bonus issues, stock splits) where cash is given instead of fractional shares; 4) Interest from State Development Loans (SDLs).  See zerodha.com/varsity/chapter/government-securities for more on G-secs.
What is Zerodha’s referral programme, an: Zerodha's referral program rewards you with 300 reward points for each successful referral (a new account opened using your referral link within 60 days).  Brokerage-based referral commissions are suspended until further notice from the exchange (as of August 25, 2024).  Reward points can be used to waive AMC or subscribe to paid partner products; they don't expire and are non-refundable.  To refer someone: On the Kite app, tap Client ID, then Invite friends, then Share. On Console, click Client ID, then Rewards & referrals, enter details, and click Submit. You can also use the referral link at zerodha.com/refer.  The referral must open an account within 60 days of registration; referrals won't be credited if the prospect registered on the website before using the referral link. Check console.zerodha.com/refer for immediate confirmation.  The referral wallet is blocked for violations of terms and conditions (see zerodha.com/tos/referrals). Referral benefits apply to new accounts from January 1, 2020.  Minors can refer, receiving only 300 reward points.
How to withdraw referral earnings?: Due to exchange regulations (as of August 25, 2024), brokerage-based referral commissions are temporarily suspended.  To withdraw referral earnings (if any remain from before the suspension): Log in to Console, click your Client ID, then Rewards & referrals, then Withdraw, and then Confirm.  A minimum of ₹1,000 is required in your referral wallet.  Reward points are non-refundable and can only be used for Zerodha partner products; see console.zerodha.com/refer.  Withdrawal requests are processed within 10 business days.
How does the referral wallet work?: Due to exchange regulations (as of August 25, 2024), brokerage-based referral commissions are temporarily suspended. Referral earnings (if any remain from before the suspension) are updated in your referral wallet by the first week of the following month (e.g., January earnings are updated in early February).  See zerodha.com/z-connect/zerodha/zerodha-associate-program/referrals-just-got-more-rewarding for more on the brokerage sharing program.  For your first withdrawal, you need at least one successful referral and ₹1,000 in earnings; subsequent withdrawals also require a minimum of ₹1,000.  Payouts are made after a 5% TDS (or applicable income tax).  Unclaimed amounts as of March 31st are reported to the ITD and carried forward to the next financial year (shown in Form 26AS).
When does the referral wallet get update: Due to exchange regulations (as of August 25, 2024), brokerage-based referral commissions are temporarily suspended.  The referral wallet is updated with a month's brokerage earnings during the first week of the following month (e.g., January earnings are updated in early February). See "How does the referral wallet work?"
Who is an Authorised Person (AP) and how: According to SEBI (WEB), an Authorised Person (AP) is an individual, firm, LLP, or corporate body appointed by a stockbroker to act on their behalf.  SEBI doesn't register or charge APs; they're approved by the stock exchange (NSE charges ₹5000 per segment + GST).  APs are supervised by the stockbroker and exchange; they can't handle client funds or securities directly. To appoint an AP, a stockbroker submits an application to the exchange.  Eligibility criteria for individuals include Indian citizenship, age 18+, no fraud/dishonesty convictions, good reputation, at least 10th-standard education, and relevant certification.  For non-individuals, all partners/directors must meet individual criteria, the entity's MoA must include securities business, and sufficient infrastructure is required.  Conditions include the stockbroker's responsibility for AP actions, no direct client interaction by the AP, remuneration solely from the stockbroker, and written agreements between the stockbroker and AP. To register as a Zerodha AP: Be an existing Zerodha client; have an organic lead source (no paid advertising or trade inducement); have at least 100 successful referrals via Zerodha's referral program; create a ticket providing contact information, lead source, entity type, and business nature.  You'll receive a response within two business days.
Do the reward points expire?: No, reward points do not expire.  They can be accumulated and used to subscribe to Zerodha partner products (see console.zerodha.com/refer); they are non-refundable. Note: Due to exchange regulations (as of August 25, 2024), brokerage-based referral commissions are temporarily suspended.  You will still receive 300 reward points for each successful referral.
How to become a Zerodha Partner?: Due to exchange regulations (as of August 25, 2024), the brokerage-based referral commission aspect of the Zerodha Partner program is temporarily suspended.  To be considered for partnership, you must have organically referred at least 100 accounts (through online or offline means, without misinformation or incentives like cashbacks), and Zerodha will contact you to verify your referrals.  See zerodha.com/tos/referrals for terms and conditions.
If the old referral account is closed an: No, if an old referral account is closed and reopened, it will not receive referral benefits.  Referral benefits apply to new accounts opened since January 1, 2020.  Note: Due to exchange regulations (as of August 25, 2024), brokerage-based referral commissions are temporarily suspended.  You will still receive 300 reward points for each successful referral.
Why was the referral not mapped even tho: A referral may not be mapped if: The prospect registered on the Zerodha website before using the referral link to open an account; the referral didn't open an account within 60 days; or the account was closed and reopened.  See zerodha.com/tos/referrals for terms and conditions.  To check referral status, log in to console.zerodha.com, click your Client ID, then Rewards & referrals, and finally View Referrals. Note: Due to exchange regulations (as of August 25, 2024), brokerage-based referral commissions are temporarily suspended.  You will still receive 300 reward points for each successful referral.
Why are withdrawal requests not being pr: Withdrawal requests may not be processed if: The referrals were added before January 2020; or one or more referral accounts were opened in the current month (only the previous month's referrals are considered for payouts).  If you have a referral this month but not last month, you can request a withdrawal the following month. See the Terms & Conditions for Referral Incentive Scheme Policy for details. Note: Due to exchange regulations (as of August 25, 2024), brokerage-based referral commissions are temporarily suspended.  You will still receive 300 reward points for each successful referral.

Due to an exchange circular (PDF) effective August 25, 2024,  brokerage-based referral commissions are temporarily suspended until further clarification. Reward points are non-refundable and can be used to waive your annual Account Maintenance Charge (AMC) or to subscribe to Zerodha's paid partner products.  Reward points do not expire. The referral must open an account within 60 days of registration; referrals will not be credited if the prospect registered on the Zerodha website before using the referral link. Can Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) invest i: Yes, provided they have an NRI account with Zerodha.  See "What documents are required to open a Zerodha account as an NRI?" for account opening information.  Note: US and Canada-based investors cannot invest in mutual funds through Coin.
What is Coin?: Coin is an online platform for buying mutual funds directly from asset management companies, with no commission fees.  All your assets (mutual funds, stocks, currencies, bonds) are held and accessible in your demat account. For more information, visit coin.zerodha.com.  The Coin app is available on the Android Play Store and iOS App Store.
Can non-individual account holders inves: Yes, using NEFT or RTGS.  To pay, click Buy, enter the amount, click Buy now, then Confirm; then make the payment via netbanking using the account details shown on Coin. Funds are transferred on a FIFO (First In First Out) basis; excess is refunded within T+4 days. Funds must come from a linked Zerodha bank account; IMPS transfers are rejected; NAV allocation depends on ICCL settlement (up to 24 hours); HDFC netbanking is instant; current accounts are accepted; one transfer covers multiple orders (but not vice versa); and orders remain open in BSE StARMF for T+5 days.  The Coin account details are unique: MFDICC006498ABXXXX (MFDICC = ICCL initials, 006498 = Zerodha's member code, ABXXXX = client login).
What are Direct Mutual Funds?: Direct mutual funds let investors buy mutual funds directly from the AMC (Asset Management Company) or fund house, without using a distributor. This eliminates distributor commissions and fees, leading to lower costs and potentially higher returns.  An AMC invests pooled funds from multiple investors into various financial instruments. A distributor acts as an intermediary between the investor and the AMC, earning a commission (e.g., a ₹1000 investment might have ₹10 deducted for the distributor). Direct plans avoid this commission, leading to higher returns compared to regular plans. See "Why is the NAV for direct mutual funds higher than regular mutual funds?" for more information.
How to pledge mutual fund investments to: Pledging mutual funds is done the same way as pledging other securities.  For instructions, see "How to pledge securities to get collateral margin?"
What are the charges applicable for inve: There are no charges for investing in mutual funds, ETFs, or mutual fund NFOs through Coin.  There are also no DP (Depository Participant) charges.  There are no additional Account Maintenance Charges (AMC) because Coin investments are held in demat form.  See "What does Depository Participant(DP) charge mean?" and "What is Account Maintenance Charge (AMC) with regard to my demat account at Zerodha?"
What are the advantages of using Coin?: Coin offers commission-free investing in direct mutual funds (avoiding commissions added to regular plans' expense ratios); step-up SIP features (automatic SIP amount increases); easy SIP management (start, pause, stop, adjust amounts); NAV order tracking with a wide fund selection; a single portfolio view of stocks and mutual funds (easily pledged for loans); consolidated statements simplifying tax deductions; easier claims by dependents in case of death; and the ability to view and compare fund investments.  See "What are Direct Mutual Funds?" and "What is step-up SIP, and how can it be set on Coin web?" for more details.
What is the difference between Coin and: Coin mandates automate fund transfers from your bank account to your BSE StAR MF ICCL account for SIPs. Console mandates automate fund transfers from your bank account to your Zerodha account for stock investments and ETF SIPs.  They are not interchangeable; a Coin mandate cannot be used for Console, and vice versa.  Both types of mandates can handle up to ₹1 crore.  See "What is a Mandate and how to create them for SIPs on Coin app?" and "How to set up automatic fund transfers from a bank account to a Zerodha trading account?" for more details.
How to check the mandate status on Coin?: Click Mandates on Coin. After registration, the status will show as Processing; within 3 business days, it will update to Successful or Failed.  Failed mandates are removed and can't be tracked.
Why is the mandate registration status n: e-mandate registration usually takes 5 business days.  If Zerodha doesn't receive bank confirmation, the status remains pending.  Zerodha follows up with banks periodically, but a specific timeline for verification can't be provided because it depends on the bank.
Why can the Coin mandate registration no: If your browser's pop-up blocker is enabled, the mandate creation page may not load. To fix this: In the Chrome Android app, click the three vertical dots (⋮), then Settings, Site settings, Pop-ups and redirects, and toggle the button to allow pop-ups; In Chrome web, click the three vertical dots (⋮), then Settings, Privacy and security, Pop-ups and redirects, and select "Sites can send pop-ups and use redirects". For Mozilla Firefox instructions, see support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/pop-blocker-settings-exceptions-troubleshooting.
Why did the Coin mandate registration fa: A Coin mandate registration may fail due to: Intermittent problems on the bank's or NPCI's website (try again later);  Digio disabling certain banks from mandate registration (check for updates to the list of disabled banks); or authentication failure (due to unsuccessful netbanking/debit card authentication, closing the authentication window prematurely, or entering incorrect credentials).  Note that failed mandates are removed and can't be tracked on the mandate page.
What are the charges for Coin mandates?: There are currently no charges for Coin mandate registration. However, banks may charge penalties for insufficient funds (amounts vary by bank).  Mandate verification charges also vary by bank (a list of charges per bank is provided in the original text; some banks do not charge).
Can clients switch between two different: No, clients cannot directly switch between schemes of the same AMC on Coin.  However, they can redeem from one scheme and then purchase another within the same AMC.  This is still considered a switch and is subject to capital gains tax, even though the funds aren't credited to your bank account.
How to activate Coin?: Coin is activated by default for all Zerodha demat account holders.  However, there are some situations where it might be inactive:  If your Zerodha account was recently opened (activation takes up to 24 hours automatically); if your account was opened before September 15, 2015 (switch your demat account from IL&FS to Zerodha - see "How to switch demat account from IL&FS to Zerodha?"); or if you opened a Zerodha trading account without a demat account (open a demat account - see "How do I open a demat account if I already have a trading or commodity account?").  Note:  Order placement requires a PAN linked to Aadhaar (see "How to link PAN with Aadhaar?").
What does IDCW on Coin mean?: IDCW stands for Income Distribution Capital Withdrawal, meaning it's a dividend distribution plan.  Mutual fund dividends are partial profit payouts from underlying investments; the NAV (Net Asset Value) decreases after the payout. For the impact of dividends on NAV, see "What is the impact of dividends on the NAV if the Income Distribution Capital Withdrawal (IDCW) scheme has paid dividends?".  Note:  Dividends are trackable on the AMC website; IDCW reinvestment isn't currently available on Coin.
Is stamp duty applicable for mutual fund: Yes, a 0.005% stamp duty applies. It's adjusted with the units allotted and not charged separately. For example, a ₹10,000 investment would have a ₹0.50 stamp duty, resulting in 999.95 units allotted at a NAV of 10. Note that stamp duty isn't currently shown under charges on Console, but this is expected to change soon.
How long will it take for mutual fund un: For liquid schemes, units are settled by 7 PM on T day and visible on Console by T+1 day. For non-liquid schemes, units are settled by 7 PM on T+1 day and visible on Console by T+2 day.  See "What is the cut-off time for mutual fund transactions on Coin and what is the applicable NAV?" for NAV and cut-off information. Note that there may be delays; see "Why are the newly allotted units shown as NA on the Coin app?" for more information.
How to add a nominee for mutual fund hol: Because Coin mutual funds are held in demat form, the nominee you've added to your demat account also applies to your mutual funds; you don't need to add a separate nominee for them.  See "How do I add a nominee online in Zerodha?" for instructions on adding a demat nominee.  To check your nominee information, go to console.zerodha.com/account/nominee. Ignore any AMC communication about nomination if a nominee is already assigned to your demat account.
Why are investments made on Coin not vis: Coin investments are held in demat form, while AMC websites typically only show folio-based investments.  Additionally, if your mobile number or email address isn't updated with the RTA (Registrar and Transfer Agent), you won't be able to log in to the AMC website. See "Why are the email id or mobile number registered with the AMC different from Coin?" for more information.
Why is the minimum initial investment fo: Coin treats SIPs as lump-sum investments made on your chosen SIP dates.  AMCs (Asset Management Companies) set minimum initial investment amounts (for the first investment) and minimum additional purchase amounts (for subsequent investments).  Coin's minimum SIP amount might be higher than on the AMC website because of this minimum initial investment requirement. For example, if the minimum initial investment is ₹5000 and the minimum additional purchase amount is ₹1000, your first SIP must be ₹5000 or more, while subsequent SIPs can be ₹1000 or more.  To avoid the higher initial investment, use AMC SIPs (set up directly via Coin).  Minimum initial investment varies across AMCs and schemes.
Why are clients unable to log in to the: Coin investments are held in demat form and may not appear on the AMC website, as it's up to the AMC whether to display demat investments. You can track these investments on Coin and via your CDSL demat holding statements (downloadable from CDSL Easi; see "How to download transaction cum holding (SOT and SOH) statement?").  ELSS statements are also downloadable on Coin (see "What are ELSS funds, and how can the ELSS statement be downloaded?").
How to change email ID or mobile number: Your AMC email and mobile number are the same as your Zerodha details, also recorded by CDSL (the depository) and shared with the RTA (Registrar and Transfer Agent). To change them, use the same method as updating your Zerodha information (see "How to change the registered mobile number or email address with Zerodha online?"). Note that RTAs update their database weekly; your demat nominee also applies to Coin investments (see "How to add a nominee to the Zerodha account online?").
Why were the funds not automatically deb: Funds may not be debited even if your SIP is linked to a mandate if: There is insufficient opening balance in your bank account on the transaction (T) day (only the T-day opening balance is considered; funds added that day don't count); or the bank rejected the fund transfer (contact your bank for details).  For example, a ₹5,000 SIP on April 5th requires sufficient funds by April 4th; adding funds on April 5th won't suffice.
What does exit load mean and how to calc: Exit loads are small penalties AMCs charge for early mutual fund redemptions. The exit load is calculated as a percentage of the NAV (Net Asset Value) at redemption, as stated in the factsheet for the investment month. For example: A ₹50,000 investment with a NAV of ₹50 results in 1000 units. If the investor redeems these 1000 units when the NAV is ₹60 and the exit load is 1%, the calculation is: (1% of ₹60) * 1000 units = ₹600; you receive ₹59,400 (₹60,000 - ₹600). For more on factsheets, see zerodha.com/varsity/chapter/the-mutual-fund-fact-sheet.
What is the impact of dividends on the N: The NAV of an IDCW (Income Distribution Capital Withdrawal) scheme will decrease by the amount of the dividend paid. For example, if the NAV before a ₹5 dividend is ₹15, the NAV after the dividend will be ₹10.
How to buy Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs)?: **On the Kite app:** Tap Bids, then Govt. securities, then Place bid, then Place bid again, and finally Submit.  **On Kite web:** Log in to kite.zerodha.com, click Bids, then Govt. securities, then Place bid; enter the amount and click Place bid.  **Important notes:** Bids from the Govt. securities section on Kite are for the primary market. Allotment takes up to 15 days after the offer closes, with an additional 15 days possible before they appear in Kite holdings. SGBs bought from Kite marketwatch (secondary market) appear on T+2 day after delivery.  An email confirms order status. Funds are debited on the last day of the order window (same-day stock sale credits are not considered). Only individuals, HUFs (Hindu Undivided Family), and trusts can buy in the primary market (corporates, partnerships, LLPs, and NRIs cannot). Fractional unit refunds are credited to your primary Zerodha-linked bank account or Zerodha account within 5-6 days of allotment.
What are ELSS funds, and how can the ELS: ELSS (Equity Linked Savings Schemes) are diversified Indian equity mutual funds offering tax benefits under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act, 1961 (up to ₹1,50,000 deduction).  They're purchased via SIP or lump sum and have a 3-year lock-in period.  Profits are taxed as LTCG (Long-Term Capital Gains). To download your ELSS statement: Log in to coin.zerodha.com, click Mutual funds, then ELSS statement, and select the financial year; or log in to console.zerodha.com/dashboard, click Reports, then Downloads, select ELSS statement, choose the financial year, and click Download (units appear after T+2 days). See "What is an SIP?", "What is a lump-sum investment?", and "How does taxation work for Mutual Fund investments?" for more details.
Where can clients learn more about inves: Video tutorials are available at "Mutual Funds Investing: A Step-by-Step Guide".  For basic information on mutual funds, visit Varsity's "Introduction to Mutual Funds – Varsity by Zerodha".  More information on mutual funds and Coin can be found at Coin Direct MF and in the Mutual Fund & ETFs section of Trading Q&A (where you can ask questions).
What is an SIP?: An SIP (Systematic Investment Plan) is a way to invest smaller amounts of money regularly (weekly, monthly, or quarterly) in mutual funds or the stock market, instead of investing a large sum at once.  This helps mitigate market volatility by buying more units at low prices and fewer at high prices.  For creating mutual fund SIPs, see "How to create a SIP on the Coin app?". For stock SIPs, see "How to create a stock SIP on Kite?"
What are Scheme Information Document (SI: A Scheme Information Document (SID) provides crucial details about a mutual fund scheme, including investment objectives, strategy, costs, asset allocation, and risks. To access the SID for a specific scheme on Coin, open the scheme's details page, scroll to the bottom, and click "Scheme document". (Visual instructions for the Coin app and Coin web are present in the original text, but not described in words).
What does NAV mean?: NAV (Net Asset Value) is the per-share price of a mutual fund or ETF.  It's calculated daily by subtracting the fund's liabilities from its assets, then dividing by the number of outstanding shares.  It represents the value of one share if the fund's assets were sold and liabilities paid.  It's the price at which investors buy and sell fund units. For more information, visit zerodha.com/varsity/chapter/concept-of-fund-nav.
How does taxation work for mutual fund i: Taxation of mutual funds depends on whether it's an equity or non-equity fund and the holding period (see the table in the original text for LTCG and STCG rates).  This information is for retail individual investors only and is subject to change; consult a Chartered Accountant (CA) before filing returns.  Dividends from non-equity schemes are paid after a 28.84% DDT (Dividend Distribution Tax), so growth schemes are generally preferred. For more on LTCG and STCG, see "What are Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) and Short-Term Capital gains (STCG), and how are they calculated?"
What is Expense ratio in mutual funds an: The expense ratio is the fee a mutual fund charges for managing your money; it's a percentage of the AUM (Assets Under Management). It's deducted from the NAV before the daily NAV is announced and is shown monthly in the factsheet on the AMC's website.  Direct plans have lower expense ratios than regular plans. For more information, see tradingqna.com/t/how-costly-are-regular-mutual-funds-compared-to-direct-plans/63599/3.

Why are mutual fund investments displaye: Close-ended mutual funds transferred to a Zerodha account appear in Kite holdings because they're exchange-traded.  Non-exchange-listed close-ended funds are visible on Console under Holdings. See "What are open ended and closed ended funds?" for more on fund types. Note: You cannot invest in close-ended mutual funds through Coin.
Why is the NAV for direct mutual funds h: Regular funds have higher expense ratios than direct funds because they pay commissions to brokers/distributors.  The expense ratio is deducted from the fund's assets before calculating the NAV.  Therefore, a higher expense ratio (like in regular funds) results in a lower NAV compared to direct funds, which have lower expense ratios. See "Introduction to Mutual Funds – Varsity by Zerodha" for more on mutual funds.
How to redeem fractional units of Liquid: Fractional Liquidbees units cannot be sold directly. You can transfer them to another demat account via CDSL easiest (see "How can I register for CDSL Easiest using my Zerodha demat account?"). To redeem them, you can either: Transfer them to the AMC's demat account using CDSL Easiest (details for Nippon India and DSP Mutual Funds are provided in the text); or fill out a Redemption Request Form (RRF) (PDF), send a soft copy via ticket for verification, and courier the form to Zerodha (address provided in the text). Redemption proceeds are credited to your linked Zerodha bank account. Note: Only fractional units are redeemed; whole units are returned to your demat account.
What does lock-in period mean?: The lock-in period is the time you can't redeem mutual fund units; it applies to ELSS (Equity Linked Savings Scheme) and retirement funds.  ELSS funds have a 3-year lock-in; retirement funds have a 5-year lock-in or until retirement.  See "What are ELSS funds and how will it help me in tax planning?".  The lock-in period is shown under holdings.
What does CAGR mean?: CAGR (Compound Annual Growth Rate) measures the annual growth rate of an investment over a period, considering compounding. It calculates the constant rate of return needed to reach the current value from the initial investment.  Unlike average annual return, it accounts for compounding, providing a smoother representation of returns over time. See zerodha.com/varsity/chapter/the-stock-markets (point 6.7) for more details.
What are open ended and closed ended fun: Open-ended funds have no limit on the number of shares they can issue; buying creates new shares, selling removes them from circulation; shares are bought/sold on demand at the daily NAV (Net Asset Value). Closed-ended funds have a fixed number of units; you can't buy units after the NFO (New Fund Offer) period; they raise capital once through an NFO; and their stock price fluctuates based on market forces and the value of their holdings.
How to get in touch with Zerodha Fund Ho: Create a ticket on their website or check their FAQs at help.zerodhafundhouse.com/support/solutions.
Why does the mutual fund NAV display T-2: Console displays the T-2 day NAV because NAV announcement times vary by scheme type (equity: 9 PM T-day; liquid: 11 PM T-day; international: 1:30 PM T+1 day). Data vendors receive and update data by the next morning; the mutual fund Bhav copy is generated at 3 PM T+1 day. Console calculates P&L using this data on the night of T+1 day, so the T+2 day holdings reflect the T-day NAV accurately.  Note: Coin shows holdings based on the T-1 day NAV.
How to calculate mutual fund returns?:
Several methods exist, depending on the investment type and duration:
* **Case 1: Lump sum investment, less than a year:** Use Absolute Return.  Absolute Return % = (Current Value - Investment Value) / Investment Value x 100.
* **Case 2: Lump sum investment, over multiple years:** Use CAGR (Compound Annual Growth Rate). CAGR = [(Current Value / Investment Value)^(365/Number of Days)] - 1. See the provided link for more on CAGR.
* **Case 3: SIP (Systematic Investment Plan), less than a year:** Use XIRR (Extended Internal Rate of Return).
* **Case 4: SIP, over a year:** Use XIRR.
Is GST included in the mutual fund expen: Yes, GST is included in the mutual fund expense ratio and doesn't need to be paid separately because money management is a service under GST purview.
What does exit load mean and how to calc: Exit loads are penalties charged by AMCs for early mutual fund redemptions. The exit load is a percentage of the NAV (Net Asset Value) at the time of redemption, as specified in the factsheet for the month of purchase.  For example: If you invested ₹50,000 at a NAV of ₹50 (getting 1000 units) and redeem at a NAV of ₹60 with a 1% exit load, the exit load is (1% of ₹60) * 1000 units = ₹600, leaving a redeemable amount of ₹59,400.  See zerodha.com/varsity/chapter/the-mutual-fund-fact-sheet for more on factsheets.

What is the applicable NAV when placing.description: The NAV used for your Coin mutual fund order depends on when ICCL (Indian Clearing Corporation Limited) receives your funds.  The cut-off times vary depending on the payment method and scheme type (see tables in the original text).
What is the applicable NAV when placing.liquid_schemes: For liquid schemes: UPI and direct settlement netbanking have a 12:30 PM cut-off (T-1 day NAV); non-direct settlement netbanking is 12 AM to 11:59 PM (T-day NAV); and NEFT/RTGS (lump sum only) is 12:30 PM (NAV may vary from T-1 to T+5 day).
What is the applicable NAV when placing.other_schemes: For other schemes (equity, debt, hybrid): UPI and direct settlement netbanking have a 2 PM cut-off (T-day NAV); non-direct settlement netbanking is 12 AM to 11:59 PM (T+1 day NAV); and NEFT/RTGS (lump sum only) is 2 PM (NAV may vary from T-day to T+5 day).
What is the applicable NAV when placing.Note: If UPI or netbanking isn't available, use NEFT/RTGS; ICCL account details will be provided.  The redemption cut-off time is 3:00 PM (T-day NAV).  See "What does Exit load mean?".  The exchange and payment aggregator determine cut-off times; if funds arrive after the cut-off, the next day's NAV is used; and to ensure a SIP starts this month, set it up by the 2nd for a 5th-of-the-month execution.  See the provided DOC for a list of supported banks.

What are covered bonds?.definition: Covered bonds represent a type of debt securities issued by banks or Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs), which are backed by a pool of assets. These bonds assure investors that in the event of the issuer's default, the funds can be recovered from the collateralized pool of assets.

Why is the mutual fund order rejected wi.description: When an account is opened with Zerodha, a Third Party Verification (TPV) is carried out for the bank accounts. Similarly, when an account is enabled on BSE STaR MF, the exchange does a TPV of the bank account and marks the bank account as valid or invalid.
Why is the mutual fund order rejected wi.resolution: Create a ticket and attach a copy of a bank statement or a cancelled cheque with the following details clearly visible: Name of the account holder, Bank account number, IFSC, Bank and branch name. Zerodha will then contact the exchange to validate the bank account, which may take up to a week. After that, fund transfers can be made while purchasing mutual funds. In the case of failed orders, the deducted funds will be refunded to the primary bank account linked with Zerodha within T+5 days.
